circumpadanus.definition: circumpadānus adj. circum + Padus, about the Po: campi, L.

circumplaudo.definition: circum - plaudō —, —, ere, to applaud all around: manibus, O.

circumplector.definition: circumplector —, ī, dep. circum + plecto, to clasp, embrace, surround, encompass: coniunctiones motu undique: domini patrimonium: pharetram auro, V.: (collem) opere, Cs.

circumplico.definition: circum-plicō āvī, ātus, āre, to wind around: anguem vectis: belua circumplicata serpentibus.

circumpono.definition: circum-pōnō posuī, —, ere, to set around, place around: nemus stagno, Ta.: piper catillis, H.: alquos curuli suae, to seat beside, Ta.

circumpotatio.definition: circumpōtātiō ōnis, f poto, a drinking around, drinking in turn, C. (XII Tables).

circumretitus.definition: circumrētitus P. circum + rete, enclosed with a net, ensnared: frequentiā populi R.

circumrodo.definition: circum-rōdō —, —, ere, to gnaw around.— Fig.: dudum enim circumrodo, quod, etc., i. e. have long hesitated to utter: Dente Theonino circumroditur, i. e. is slandered, H.

circumsaepio.definition: circum-saepiō (not -sēp-), saepsī, saeptus, īre, to hedge round, fence around, encircle, enclose: circumsaeptus lectis hominum viribus: armatis corpus, L. — In tmesis: Classis Aggeribus saepta circum, V. — Fig.: vos ī…

circumscindo.definition: circum-scindō —, —, ere, to rend around, strip (once): aliquem, L.

circumscribo.definition: circum-scrībō īpsī, īptus, ere, to encircle, circumscribe, enclose in a ring: orbem: virgulā stantem: virgā regem, L. — Fig., to define, encompass, enclose, limit, bound, circumscribe: nullis terminis ius suum: genus …

circumscripte.definition: circumscrīptē adv. circumscriptus, in periods: dicere: complecti singulas res.

circumscriptio.definition: circumscrīptiō ōnis, f circumscribo, a boundary, circle, limit, outline, contour, circuit, compass: terrae: temporis. — In rhet., a period: verborum.—Fig., a deceiving, cheating, overreaching, defrauding: adulescentiu…

circumscriptor.definition: circumscrīptor ōris, m circumscribo, a defrauder, deceiver, cheat, C.: ad iura vocare Circumscriptorem, Iu.

circumscriptus.definition: circumscrīptus adj. P. of circumscribo.— In rhet., in periods, periodic: verborum ambitūs.

circumseco.definition: circum-secō —, —, āre, to cut around: aliquid serrulā , to saw around.

circumsedeo.definition: circum-sedeō sēdī, sessus, ēre, to sit around, surround, besiege, blockade, invest, encompass, beset: Mutinam: te in castello: oppidum, S.: in castello circumsederi, N.: opem circumsessis ferre, L.— Fig., to surround,…

circumsessio.definition: circumsessiō ōnis, f circumsedeo, a hostile encompassing, besieging.

circumsido.definition: circum-sīdō —, —, ere, to besiege: Plistiam, L.: oppidum, S.

circumsilio.definition: circumsiliō —, —, īre circum + salio, to leap around, dance around: circumsilit Morborum omne genus, Iu.

circumsisto.definition: circum-sistō stetī or stitī, —, ere (in perf. like circumsto), to take one's stand around, surround, stand around: hominem, Cs.: cum singulas binae naves circumsteterant, Cs.: curiam, L.: sex lictores circumsistunt: c…

circumsono.definition: circum-sonō —, —, āre, to sound, resound on every side: locus circumsonat ululatibus, is filled, L.: ad circumsonans clamor, L. — To surround with sound, make to resound, fill with sound: aurīs vocibus undique: clamor…

circumsonus.definition: 'circum-sonus adj., sounding around, filling with sound: turba canum, barking around, O.'

circumspectio.definition: circumspectiō ōnis, f circumspicio, foresight, circumspection, caution: aliqua.

circumspecto.definition: circumspectō āvī, ātus, āre, intens. circumspicio, to look about with attention, search around, look after: bestiae ut in pastu circumspectent: ora principum, L.: omnia: mare et silvas, Ta.: quānam ipse evaderet, L.: …

circumspectus1.definition: 'circumspectus adj. P. of circumspicio, well considered, guarded: verba, O.'

circumspectus2.definition: circumspectus ūs, m circumspicio, a looking about, regarding: ut distineret regem ab circumspectu rerum aliarum, consideration, L.—A view around, outlook: facilis est circumspectus, unde exeam: eo, unde circumspectus …

circumspicio.definition: circumspiciō ēxī (perf. circumspēxtī, T.), ectus, ere circum + specio, to look about, cast a look around, observe, see: circumspicio; nusquam (sc. te video), T.: coniunx ubi sit, O.: nec suspicit nec circumspicit: nus…

circumsto.definition: circum-stō stetī, —, āre (in perf. like circumsisto), to stand around, take place around: spe praedae adducti circumsteterunt, Cs.: circumstant properi aurigae, V.: circumstantes silvae, O.—To surround, encompass, enc…

circumstrepo.definition: circum-strepō tius, ere circum + strepo, to make a noise around, din about: clamore seditiosorum circumstrepitur, Ta.—To shout clamorously around: atrociora, Ta.

circumtero.definition: circum - terō —, —, ere, to crowd around: hunc, Tb.

circumtextus.definition: 'circum-textus adj., woven around: velamen acantho, V.'

circumtono.definition: circum-tonō uī, —, āre, to thunder around: Hunc, H.

circumvado.definition: circum-vādō vāsī, —, ere, to attack on every side, encompass, beset: naves, L. — Fig.: terror cum circumvassiset aciem, had overwhelmed, L.

circumvagus.definition: 'circum-vagus adj., wandering about, flowing around: oceanus, H.'

circumvallo.definition: circum-vāllō āvī, ātus, āre, to surround with a wall, circumvallate, blockade, invest, encompass: circumvallare loci natura prohibebat, Cs.: castra, L.: Tot res circumvallant, beset, T.

circumvectio.definition: circumvectiō ōnis, f circumveho, a carrying around— Solis, the circuit, revolution.

circumvector.definition: circumvector —, ārī, dep. circumveho, to ride about, sail around: oram, L.—Poet., to go through, describe: Singula, V.

circumvehor.definition: circum - vehor vectus, ī, to ride around, sail around: classe ad Romanum agrum, L.: navibus circumvecti milites, Cs.: per infima clivi, L.: collibus, Cs.: Brundisii promunturium, L.: circumvehens Peloponnesum, N.: han…

circumvelo.definition: circum - vēlō —, —, āre, to veil, envelop, enfold: aurato circumvelatur amictu, O.

circumvenio.definition: circum-veniō vēnī, ventus, īre, to come around, be around, encircle, encompass, surround: circumventi flammā, Cs.: Cocytos circumvenit, V.: planities locis paulo superioribus circumventa, S.: singulas urbīs, to go fro…

circumverto.definition: circum-vertō —, —, ere, to turn around, revolve on: rota circumvertitur axem, O.

circumvestio.definition: circum-vestiō —, —, īre, to clothe, cover over. —Of language: se circumvestire dictis, C. poet.

circumvolito.definition: circum - volitō āvī, —, āre, to fly around: lacūs circumvolitavit hirundo, V.: thyma, H.: circumvolitantes alites, Ta.

circumvolo.definition: circum - volō āvī, ātus, āre, to fly around: praedam, V.: mors atris circumvolat alis, H.: Spem suam, his prey, O.

circumvolvo.definition: circum-volvō —, —, ere, to roll around, revolve through: magnum sol circumvolvitur annum, V.: rota perpetuum circumvolvitur axem, O.

circus.definition: circus ī, m CVR-, a circular line, circle: lacteus, the Milky Way.— An enclosure for athletic games, race-course, ring: longo decedere circo, V.: munera circo locantur In medio, V.: maritimus (at Anagnia), L. — Esp.: …

ciris.definition: cīris is, f, kei=ris, a sea - bird, into which Scylla was changed, O.

cirrus.definition: cirrus ī, m a lock, curl, ringlet, tuft of hair, Iu.—A fringe (on a tunic), Ph.

cis.definition: 'cis praep. 2 CA-, on this side: cis Tiberim redire, L.: Euphratem: cis Rhenum incolunt, Cs.'

cisium.definition: cisium ī, n a light two-wheeled vehicle, cabriolet.

cista.definition: cista ae, f, ki/sth, a woven basket, wickerwork basket, box, T., C., Ct., Tb., O.—For books, Iu. —A money-chest: effracta, H.

cistella.definition: cistella ae, f dim. cista, a small chest, box, T.

cisterna.definition: cisterna ae, f a cistern (for water), Ta.

cistophorus.definition: cistophorus (-os) ī (gen plur. ūm, L.), m, kistofo/ros, an Asiatic coin stamped with a cista, worth about four drachmas.

citatus.definition: citātus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of 2 cito, quick, rapid, speedy, swift, in haste, at full speed: equo citato, at full gallop, Cs.: ora citatorum equorum, V.: nautae, Pr.: citato gradu, L.: axe, Iu.: citatiore agmi…

citerior.definition: citerior ōris, and citimus, adj. comp. and sup. citer from cis, on this side: citerior provincia, Cs.: Hispania, C., N.—Nearer, next: (stella) ultima a caelo, citima terris.—Fig.: humana et citeriora considerat: ut ad…

cithara.definition: cithara ae, f, kitha/ra, the cithara, cithern, guitar, lute, V., H.: citharae peritus, Ta. — The music of the cithara, art of playing on the lute: Apollo citharam dabat, V.: citharam docere alqm, Pr.

citharista.definition: citharista ae, m, kitharisth/s, a player on the cithara.

citharistria.definition: citharistria ae, f, kithari/stria, a female player on the cithara, T.

citharizo.definition: citharīzō —, —, āre, v.n., kithari/zw, to play on the cithara, N.

citharoedus.definition: citharoedus ī, m, kitharw|do/s, one who sings to the accompaniment of the cithara, C., H.

cito1.definition: cito (old citō) adv. with comp. citius, and sup. citissimē citus, quickly, speedily, soon: abi, T.: discere: dicta Percipere, H.: tacitus citius audies, T.: obrepere eam (senectutem) citius quam putavissent: non vis c…

cito2.definition: citō āvī, ātus, āre, intens. cieo, to put in quick motion, rouse, excite, only in P. perf.; see citatus.—To urge, call, summon: patres in curiam citari, L.: centuriatim populum, L.: iudices: citari nominatim unum ex i…

citra.definition: citrā adv. and praep. citer. I. Adv, on this side, on the hither side: (dextera) nec citra mota nec ultra, neither this way nor that, O.—On this side, nearer: id a capite arcessere: saepe etiam citra licet, not so far…

citreus.definition: 'citreus adj. citrus, of the citrus-tree, of citrus-wood: mensa: sub trabe, H.'

citro.definition: citrō adv. dat. of citer, to this side; only in the phrase ultro citroque, ultro et citro, or, ultro citro, hither and thither, this way and that, here and there, to and fro, backwards and forwards, reciprocally: ultr…

citus.definition: 'citus adj. P. of cieo, quick, swift, rapid: classis, H.: navis, O.: mors, H.: incessus, S.: via, L.: quadrigae, V.: solvite vela citi (i. e. cito), V.: citus denatat, H.: ite citi, O.: equo, Ta.: remis, Ta.'

civicus.definition: cīvicus adj. civis, of citizens, civil, civic: iura, H.: rabies, H.: bella, O.: arma pro trepidis reis, i. e. defence, O.: corona, the civic crown (of oak-leaves, given for saving the life of a citizen in war), C., L.

civilis.definition: cīvīlis e, adj. with comp. civis, of citizens, civil, civic: bellum: discordia, S.: acies, O.: aestus, H.: victoria, N.: mos consuetudoque: clamor, L.: quercus (i. e. corona civica), V.—As subst n.: si quicquam in vob…

civiliter.definition: cīvīliter adv. civilis, citizen-like, as becomes a private citizen: vivere: vim facere: cenare, with decent hospitality, Iu.: Exercet plus quam civiliter iras, excessively, O.

civis.definition: cīvis is, abl. -vī or -ve, m and f 2 CI-, a citizen (opp. peregrinus): Romanus: bonus et fortis: impii: cives cum civibus de virtute certabant, S.: Attica, T.: Romana: O cives, cives! my fellow-citizens, H.: trepidos …

civitas.definition: cīvitās ātis (gen plur. -ātium or -ātum), f civis, the condition of a citizen, citizenship, freedom of the city, membership in the community: populi R.: donare alqm civitate: asciscere in civitatem, L.: recipere in ci…

clades.definition: clādēs (clādis, L.) is, f 1 CEL-, destruction, injury, mischief, harm, misfortune, disaster, loss, detriment, calamity: importuna civitatis: Luctifica: magna, S.: captae urbis, L.: agrum omni belli clade pervastat, L.…

clam.definition: clam 2 CAL-, adv. and praep. I. Adv, secretly, privately, covertly, in secret: Si sperat fore clam, will not be found out, T.: tum id clam, he kept it a secret, T.: vel vi, vel clam, vel precario, by fraud, T.: Sychae…

clamator.definition: clāmātor ōris, m clamo, a bawler, declaimer.

clamito.definition: clāmitō āvī, ātus, āre, freq. clamo, to cry aloud, bawl, vociferate: (passer) vano clamitans, Ph.: quid clamitas? T.: haec, L.: Me sycophantam, call, T.: clamitans, ‘Indignum facinus,’ T.: clamitas: ‘quo usque ista di…

clamo.definition: clāmō āvī, ātus, āre 1 CAL-, intrans, to call, cry out, shout aloud, complain aloud: Non clamas? non insanis? T.: de pecuniā : anseres, qui clamant: (cicada) clamare occoepit, Ph.— Trans, to call aloud, call upon, pro…

clamor.definition: clāmor ōris, m 1 CAL-, a loud call, shout, cry: clamorem audivi, T.: tollere: ad aethera, V.: profundere: compesce, H.: magnus, S.: ingens, V.: nauticus, V.: it clamor eaelo, V. — A friendly shout, acclamation, applau…

clamosus.definition: clāmōsus adj. clamor, clamorous, full of noise: pater, Iu.: circus, resounding, Iu.: Phasma Catulli, the noisy farce, ‘the Ghost,’ Iu.

clanculum.definition: clanculum adv. and praep. clam. I. Adv, secretly, privately: mordere, T.: id agere inter se, T. — II. Praep. with acc: clanculum Patres, in secret from, T.

clandestinus.definition: clandestīnus adj. clam, secret, hidden, concealed, clandestine: scelus: nuntii legationesque, Cs.: foedus, L.: colloquia cum hostibus.

clangor.definition: clangor ōris, m 1 CAL-, a sound, clang, noise: tubarum, V.: clangorem fundere (of birds), C. poët.: consonus (pennarum), O.: cum magno clangore volitare, L.

clare.definition: clārē adv. with comp. clarus, brightly: fulgens, Ct. — Clearly, distinctly, plainly: gemere: dicere, H.: clare, ‘tuemini,’ inquit, Cs. — Fig., illustriously, honorably, splendidly: clarius exsplendescebat, N.: clarius…

clareo.definition: clāreō —, —, ēre clarus, to be bright, shine (of the stars), C. poet. — Fig., to be renowned, be illustrious: viri gloria claret, Enn. ap. C.

claresco.definition: clārēscō —, —, ēre, inch. clareo, to grow bright, Ta.—Fig., to become audible, sound clear: sonitūs armorum, V.— To become illustrious, grow famous: facinore, Ta.

clarigatio.definition: clārigātiō ōnis, f a fine, ransom (for transgressing limits), L.

clarisonus.definition: clārisonus adj. clarus + SON-, clear-sounding, loud: vox, Ct.: aurae, C. poet.

claritas.definition: clāritās ātis, f clarus.—Prop., brightness, splendor; hence, of sound, clearness: in voce.— Of reputation, celebrity, renown, fame, splendor: num te claritatis paenitebat? pro tuā claritate: claritate praestantes, N.:…

claritudo.definition: clāritūdō inis, f clarus, brightness: deae (i. e. lunae), Ta.—Renown, celebrity, splendor, fame: summa, S.: tanta, S.

claro.definition: clārō —, —, āre clarus, to make bright, exhibit, C. poet. — Fig., to illustrate, make famous, H.

clarus.definition: clārus adj. with comp. and sup. 1 CAL-, clear, bright, shining, brilliant: lux, open day: clarissimā luce laetari: mundi lumina, V.: lucerna, H.: nox, Ta.: pater clarus intonat, in the clear sky, V.: clarissimae gemma…

classiarius.definition: classiārius adj. classis, of the navy: centurio, captain of a ship, Ta.—Plur m. as subst, marines, naval forces, Cs., N.

classicula.definition: classicula ae, f dim. classis, a flotilla, little fleet.

classicum.definition: classicum ī, n classicus, a field signal, trumpet-call: cecinit, L.: cani iubet, Cs.: classico ad contionem convocat, L.: classica sonant, V.: excitatur classico miles, H.: necdum audierant inflari classica, trumpets, V.

classicus.definition: classicus adj. classis, of the fleet, of the navy: milites, marines, L.: bella, naval, Pr.: legio, Ta.—Plur m. as subst, marines, Ta.

classis.definition: classis is (abl. e; rarely ī), f 1 CAL-, a class, great division (of the people, formed, according to property, by Servius Tullius), L.: prima classis vocatur ... tum secunda classis, etc.—Fig.: quintae classis videri…

clatra.definition: clātra ōrum, n (Pr.), or clātrī (-thrī), ō rum, m (H.), klh=thra, a lattice, grate, bars.

claudicatio.definition: claudicātiō ōnis, f claudico, a limping, C.

claudico.definition: claudicō —, —, āre, v. n. claudus, to limp, halt, be lame: ex volnere.—Fig., to halt, waver, be wanting, be defective: tota res claudicat: in ullo officio: si quid in nostrā oratione claudicat.

claudo1.definition: claudō (clūdō) sī, sus, ere CLAV-, to shut, close, shut up: forem cubiculi: portas, Cs.: rivos, to dam up, V.: clausae fores, Tb.: ostia, Ct.: ocellos, Pr.: clausae hieme Alpes, L.: pupulas: lumina, V.—Fig., to shut, …

claudo2.definition: claudō —, —, ēre CLAV-. — Prop., to limp; hence, fig., to falter, hesitate, stumble: etiam si (vita) ex aliquā parte clauderet: quid est cur claudere orationem malint?: si alterā parte claudet res p., L.

claudus.definition: claudus adj. CLAV-, limping, halting, lame: deus: altero pede, N.: pes, H.: pars serpentis, V. —Prov.: claudus pilam, the lame man (holds fast) the ball.—Fig., crippled, imperfect, defective: naves, L.—Of language: ca…

claustra.definition: claustra ōrum, n claudo, a lock, bar, bolt: revellere claustra: rumpere, V.: portarum, L.: sub claustris rei p. positum vectigal.—A barrier, bounds: obstantia rumpere claustra (the barriers of a race - course), H. — A…

claustrum.definition: claustrum ī, n claudo, rare collat. form of claustra, a barrier, hindrance: obicitur, i. e. a chain, Cu.—A frontier fortress, key, point of control: iam perdomitorum, Cu.

clausula.definition: clausula ae, f claudo, a close, conclusion, end: in quo (mimo), a fitting end: epistulae.—In rhet., the close of a period.

clausum.definition: clausum ī, n claudo, an enclosure: in clauso linquere, in confinement, V.

clausus.definition: clausus adj. P. of claudo, close, reserved, Ta.

clava.definition: clāva ae, f 1 CEL-, a knotty branch, rough stick, cudgel, club: sternentes agmina clavā, V.: male mulcati clavis: Herculea, Pr. — A foil (for exercise).

clavarium.definition: clāvārium ī, n clavus, money given to soldiers to buy shoe-nails, Ta.

clavicula.definition: clāvicula ae, f dim. clavus, a tendril.

claviger1.definition: clāviger gera, gerum, adj. clava + GES-, club-bearing: Volcani proles, i. e. Periphetes, O.— Of Hercules, the club-bearer, O.

claviger2.definition: clāviger gerī, m clavis + GES-, the keybearer (of Janus), O.

clavis.definition: clāvis is (abl. vī or ve), f CLAV-, a key: horreorum claves: clavī s portis imposuit, L.: portarum, Iu.: adulterinae portarum, false keys, S.: clavī s adimere (uxori), to divorce.—A bolt: clavīs portis imponere, L.— A…

clavus.definition: clāvus ī, m CLAV-, a nail: clavi ferrei, Cs.: clavos figentes, L.: clavo ab dictatore fixo, L.: ex hoc die clavum anni movebis, i. e. reckon the beginning of the year: tamquam clavo clavum eiciendum: beneficium trabal…

clemens.definition: clēmēns entis (abl. -tī; rarely -te, L.), adj. with comp. and sup, mild, calm, gentle: clementissimus amnis, O.—Fig., calm, quiet, gentle, tranquil, kind: vita, T.: cupio me esse clementem: satis in disputando.— Mild,…

clementer.definition: clēmenter adv. with comp. clemens, quietly, placidly, tranquilly, calmly: si quid est factum clementer: hominem accepit.—By degrees, gradually: iuga clementius adire, Ta.: editum iugum, Ta. —With forbearance, mildly, …

clementia.definition: clēmentia ae, f clemens, moderation, mildness, forbearance, benignity, clemency, mercy: clementiā in eos uti, Cs.: nihil magno viro dignius clementiā : victoris: monimentum clementiae suae: clementiā concordiam ordinu…

clepo.definition: clepō psī, —, ere CLEP-, to steal (rare): sacrum qui clepsit (for clepserit): si quis clepsit, etc., L. (old law).

clepsydra.definition: 'clepsydra ae, f, kleyu/dra, an instrument for measuring time by water, water-glass, waterclock, clepsydra ; used to measure the time of a speaker; hence, cras ergo ad clepsydram, by the clock (of exercises in declama…

cliens.definition: cliēns entis (gen plur. -entium; rarely -entum, H.), m for cluens, P. of clueo, a personal dependant, client (a freeman, protected by a patron; he received from him an allotment of land or of food, and accompanied him…

clienta.definition: clienta ae, f cliens, a female client, H.

clientela.definition: clientēla ae, f cliens, clientship, patronage, protection, the relation of a client to his patron: in clientelam Nobis dedit se, T.: in cuius fide sint et clientelā, whose clients they are.—Plur., clients, dependants:…

clientulus.definition: clientulus ī, m dim. cliens, a poor client, Ta

clinatus.definition: clīnātus adj. CLI-, bent, sunk, C. poet.

clipeatus.definition: clipeātus adj. clipeus, armed with a shield, shield-bearing: agmina, V.: seges virorum, O.— Plur. as subst: adversus clipeatos, L.

clipeus.definition: clipeus (clup-) ī, m, or clipeum, ī, n CLEP-, a round shield of metal: speciem inclusit in clupeo: maximis clipeis uti, N.: clipeos ad tela sinistris obicere, V.—Prov.: clipeum post volnera sumere, i. e. to act too la…

clitellae.definition: clītellae ārum, f CLI-, a pack-saddle, sumpter-saddle: clitellis alqd apportare: clitellas ponere, H.: mihi imponere, Ph.

clitellarius.definition: clītellārius adj. clitellae, bearing a packsaddle: mulus, C., L., H., Ph.

clivosus.definition: clīvōsus adj. clivus, hilly, full of hills (poet.): rus, V.— Steep, arduous: Latina (via), Iu.: Olympus, O.

clivus.definition: clīvus or clīvos ī, m CLI-, a declivity, slope, ascent, hill, eminence: Clivos deorsum vorsum est, T.: adversus clivum, up-hill, Cs.: erigere in primos agmen clivōs, the foot-hills, L.: Viribus uteris per clivō s, H.:…

cloaca.definition: cloāca ae, f 2 CLV-, a canal for waste liquids, sewer, drain, C.: alqd in cloacam iacere, H.: maxima, the great sewer draining the Aventine, Capitoline, and Palatine hills, L.

clueo.definition: clueō —, —, ēre 1 CLV-, to hear, be spoken of, be said (old): ignis cluet mortalibus clam divisus, Att. ap. C.

clunis.definition: clūnis m and f a buttock, haunch.—Plur., L., Iu.: sine clune palumbes (the choicest parts), H.

coacervatio.definition: coacervātiō ōnis, f coacervo.—In rhet., an accumulation (of proofs, etc.): universa.

coacervo.definition: coacervō āvī, ātus, āre com- + acervo, to heap together, heap up, collect in a mass: pecuniae coacervantur: tantam vim emblematum: cadavera, Cs.: hostium cumulos, L.: agros, to amass. —Fig., to multiply, heap: argumen…

coacesco.definition: coacēscō acuī, —, ere, inch. com- + acesco, to become acid, sour: ut vinum, sic aetas vetustate coacescit.—Fig., to deteriorate, become corrupt.

coacta.definition: coācta ōrum, n cogo, felted cloths, Cs.

coactor.definition: coāctor ōris, m cogo, a collector (of money): perquiritur a coactoribus.— In an army, the rearguard: coactores agminis, Ta.

coactus2.definition: (coāctus ūs), m cogo, compulsion, constraint (only abl sing.): coactu istius, under compulsion from him: civitatis, Cs.: meo.

coaedifico.definition: coaedificō —, ātus, āre com- + aedifico, to build up, build upon: campum: loci coaedificati.

coaequo.definition: coaequō āvī, ātus, āre com- + aequo, to make equal, make even, level: montes, S.—Fig., to equalize, drag down: ad libidines tuas omnia.

coagmentatio.definition: coāgmentātiō ōnis, f coagmento, a joining, connection, union: corporis: non dissolubilis.

coagmento.definition: coāgmentō āvī, ātus, āre coagmentum, to join, cement together, connect: trabes, Cs.: opus suum (natura).—Fig., to connect: verba: (verborum) concursus coagmentatus: pacem, to conclude.

coagmentum.definition: coāgmentum ī, n cogo, a joining together, joint: inter coagmenta lapidum, Cs.

coagulum.definition: coāgulum ī, n cogo, an agent of coagulation, rennet, runnet, O.—Curds: liquefacta coagula lacte, O.

coalesco.definition: coalēscō aluī, alitus, ere, inch. com- + 1 AL-, to grow firmly, strike root, increase, become strong: ilex coaluerat inter saxa, had sprung up, S.: in cortice ramus, O.—Fig., to unite, agree together, coalesce: Troian…

coangusto.definition: coangustō —, —, āre com- +angustus, to limit, restrict: legem.

coarguo.definition: coarguō uī, —, ere com- + arguo, to overwhelm with proof, refute, silence, expose, convict, prove guilty: refelli, coargui putat esse turpissimum: tot testibus coargui: Lentulum dissimulantem coarguunt sermonibus, S.:…

coartatio.definition: coartātiō (coarct-) ōnis, f coarto, a crowding, pressing together: plurium in angusto, L.

coarto.definition: coartō (-arctō) āvī, ātus, āre com- + arto, to press together, compress, contract, confine: angustae fauces coartant iter, L.: in oppidis coartatus. —Fig., to abridge, shorten: consulatum, Ta.: iter, O.—Of discourse, …

coccum.definition: coccum ī, n, ko/kkos, a berry yielding a scarlet dye: rubro cocco tingere, with scarlet, H.

coclea.definition: 'coclea (cochlea), ae, f, koxli/as, a snail: inter saxa repentes, S.: Afra, H.'

coctilis.definition: 'coctilis e, adj. coquo, burned: laterculi, Cu.: muri, of burned bricks, O.'

codex.definition: cōdex icis, m (for caudex), a block: Codice misso, O.—A log for punishing slaves, stocks: inmundus, Pr.: residens in codice, Iu. — A block sawn into tablets, book, writing, manuscript, document (in leaves; cf. volumen…

codicilli.definition: cōdicillī ōrum, m dim. codex, a writingtablet, note-book: sententias in codicillos referre. —A note, billet, C.: codicillos ferre cum praecepto, Ta.—A petition, Ta. — An imperial rescript, patent, Ta.— A will, testame…

coemo.definition: coëmō ēmī, ēmptus, ere com- + emo, to purchase, buy up, forestall: multa, T.: carrorum numerum, Cs.: res pretiosas: frumentum, Iu.

coemptio.definition: coēmptiō ōnis, f coëmo.—In law, a form of marriage by a pretended sale, transferring the woman, with her estate, to the man (in manum).— A fictitious marriage (to free an heiress from special burdens).

coeo.definition: coëō īvī or iī, itus, īre com- + eo, to go together, come together, meet, assemble, collect: in Piraeo, T.: matronae ad Venturiam frequentes coëunt, L.: quo populus coibat, H.: certis diebus (ad concilium), Ta.: milia…

coepio.definition: (coepiō) coepī, coeptus, ere com- + 1 AP-, to begin, commence: non Prius olfecissem, quam ille quicquam coeperet? T.: mecum cogitare, T.: cum ver esse coeperat: Fluctus coepit albescere, V.: oppugnare, Cs.: alia fieri…

coepto.definition: coeptō —, —, āre, intens, coepio, to begin eagerly, begin, undertake, attempt: contingere portūs, C. (poet.): appetere ea. quae, etc.: quid coeptas, Thraso? T.: insidias, Ta.

coeptum.definition: coeptum ī, n coepio, a work begun, beginning, undertaking: nec taedia coepti Ulla mei capiam, O.: audax, L.: audacibus adnue coeptis, V.: temere coepta, L.: coeptis meis, O.: ne enuntiare coepta, L.

coeptus2.definition: (coeptus ūs), m coepio, a beginning, undertaking.—Only plur: suos.

coerceo.definition: coërceō cuī, citus, ēre com- + arceo, to enclose on all sides, hold together, surround, encompass: (mundus) omnia coërcet: Vitta coercebat capillos, O.: virgā coërces turbam, H. — To restrain, confine, shut in, hold, …

coercitio.definition: coërcitiō ōnis, f coërceo, a restraining, restraint, compulsion, chastisement: coërcitionem inhib<*>re, L.: magistratūs, on the part of the magistrates, L.: sine coërcitionibus agere, Ta.

coetus.definition: coetus ūs, m for coitus, a coming together: amnium, Cu.—An assemblage, crowd, company: in omni coetu concilioque: sollemnes ludorum: nocturni, L.: socios in coetum Advocat, V.: coetu soluto, O.: coetibus alqd sancire,…

cogitate.definition: cōgitātē adv. cogito, with reflection, considerately: quae scripsisset.

cogitatio.definition: cōgitātiō ōnis, f cogito, a thinking, considering, deliberating, thought, reflection, meditation, imagination: cogitatio in se ipsā vertitur: commentatio et cogitatio: acerrima et attentissima: simplices, magnas, Ta.:…

cogitatum.definition: cōgitātum ī, n cogito, a thought, reflection, notion, idea: acutius imperatoris, N.—Usu. plur: cogitata proloqui, T.: eloqui: patefacere, purpose, N.: sapientium.

cogitatus.definition: cōgitātus adj. P. of cogito, deliberate: iniuria: verbum.

cogito.definition: cōgitō āvī, ātus, āre com- + agito, to consider thoroughly, ponder, weigh, reflect upon, think: etiam atque etiam, T.: animo, T.: rationem: maiores vestros, Ta.: te video, non cogito solum: Scipionem, to call to mind:…

cognata.definition: cōgnāta ae, f 1 cognatus, a female relation, kinswoman: ne in cognatam pecces, T.: tuae, T.

cognatio.definition: cōgnātiō ōnis, f 1 cognatus, blood-relationship, kindred, connection by birth: frater noster cognatione patruelis: te maxime cognatione attingebat: cognationem intervenisse, S.: propinquā cognatione Hannibali iunctus,…

cognatus1.definition: cōgnātus adj. com- + GEN-, sprung from the same stock, related by blood, kindred: mihi: patres, the relationship of our fathers, V.: per cognata corpora supplex, as a kinsman, O.: anguilla cognata colubrae, Iu.—Of a k…

cognatus2.definition: cognātus ī, m 1 cognatus, a kinsman, blood-relation: his proximus, T.: amici cognatique alcius: est tibi mater, Cognati? H.: cognatorum aliquis, Iu.

cognitio.definition: cōgnitiō ōnis, f com- + GNA-, a becoming acquainted with, acquiring knowledge, knowledge, acquaintance: rerum: animi: urbis: cognitione atque hospitio dignus.—A conception, notion, idea: deorum innatae cognitiones. — …

cognitor.definition: cōgnitor ōris, m com- + GNA-.—In law, an advocate, attorney: cognitorem ascribit Sthenio: qui cognitor est datus: qui cognitores homines honestos daret, was represented by: iuris sui: ire domum iube, fi cognitor ipse,…

cognitus.definition: cōgnitus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of cognosco, known, acknowledged, approved: res plane: homo virtute cognitā: cognitiora (mala), O.: haec esse cognitissima, Ct.: nulli cognitius, O.

cognomen.definition: cōgnōmen inis, n com- + GNA-, a surname, second-name, family-name (added to the name of the gens to distinguish the family): T. Manlius, qui Galli torque detracto cognomen (sc. Torquati) invenit: sapientis: Crassus co…

cognomentum.definition: cōgnōmentum ī, n rare or late for cognomen, a surname: cognomento qui skoteino\s perhibetur, Poet. ap. C.: Puteoli cognomentum a Nerone adipiscuntur, Ta.—A name: (Rhenum) verso cognomento Vahalem dicere, Ta.

cognominis.definition: (cōgnōminis e), only abl sing., cognomine, adj. cognomen, like-named, of the same name: cognomine Insubribus pago, bearing the same name, L.: gaudet cognomine terrā, V.

cognosco.definition: cōgnōscō gnōvī (often contr., cōgnō stī, cōgnōrō, cōgnōsse, etc.), gnitus, ere com- + (g)nōscō, to become acquainted with, acquire knowledge of, ascertain, learn, perceive, understand ; perf., to know: regiones, Cs.: …

cogo.definition: cōgō coēgī, coāctus, ere com- + ago, to drive together, collect, crowd, bring together, summon, congregate, convene: certe cogit is qui congregat homines: coacti sunt si, etc.: pecus, V.: talenta ad quindecim Coë gi, …

cohaerens.definition: cohaerēns ntis, adj. P. of cohaereo, adjoining, continuous: aedificia, Ta. — Fig., consistent: apta inter se et cohaerentia: non cohaerentia inter se dicere, inconsistent assertions. — Harmonious: oratio.

cohaerentia.definition: 'cohaerentia ae, f cohaereo, a coherence, connection: mundi.'

cohaereo.definition: cohaereō haesī, haesus, ēre com- + haereo, to cling together, be united, cohere: mundus apte cohaeret. — To consist of, be composed of: alia quibus cohaererent homines. — In thought, to be consistent, agree together: …

cohaeresco.definition: cohaerēscō —, —, ere, inch. cohaereo, to hang together, cohere: atomi inter se.

coheres.definition: cohērēs ēdis, m and f com- + heres, a coheir, fellow-heir, sharer in an inheritance, C.: filio coheredes alquos adiungere: esse alicui, H.

cohibeo.definition: cohibeō uī, (itus), ēre com- + habeo, to hold together, hold, contain, confine, embrace, comprise: omnīs naturas: Scyllam caecis cohibet spelunca latebris, V.: nodo crinem, H.: marem cohibent (ova) vitellum, H.: auro …

cohonesto.definition: co-honestō āvī, ātus, āre com- + honesto, to honor in common, do honor to, honor, grace: exsequias: statuas: aliquid virtute, L.: funus laudatione, Ta.

cohorresco.definition: co-horrēscō horruī, —, ēre, inch. com- + horresco, to shudder, shiver: equidem cohorrui: ex quo (sudore): quod litterae tuae adferrent, etc.

cohors.definition: cohors rtis (acc. cortem, C.), f com- + HER-, a court, enclosure, yard, pen, cattle-yard, O.: habes cortem in Palatio, i. e. your house.—A crowd, multitude, company, throng, train: gigantum, H.: fratrum stipata, V.: i…

cohortatio.definition: cohortātiō ōnis, f cohortor, an exhorting, inciting, exhortation, encouragement: militum, N.: legionis, Cs.: iudicum ad honeste iudicandum: concitatus cohortatione alicuius ad alqd. — Plur., Cs., C.

cohortor.definition: co-hortor ātus, ārī, dep. com- + hortor, to animate, encourage, advise, incite, exhort, admonish: hac (eloquentiā) cohortamur: vim habere ad cohortandum: vos ad libertatem recuperandam: nostri cohortati inter se, Cs.:…

coinquino.definition: co-inquinō —, —, āre, to pollute, contaminate: matres coinquinari regum, Att. ap. C.

coitio.definition: coitiō ōnis, f coëo, a coming together, meeting: prima, T.: absterrere singulos a coitionibus, L.—A conspiracy, plot, coalition: suspitio coitionis: coitiones tribunorum adversus inventutem, L.: coitionem facere.

coitus.definition: coitus ūs, m com- + 1 I-, sexual union, O.

colaphus.definition: colaphus ī, m, ko/lafos, a blow with the fist, cuff, box on the ear: quingentos colaphos infregit mihi, T.: colaphum incutimus servo, Iu.

colax.definition: 'colax acis, m a flatterer: parasitus colax, T.'

colens.definition: colēns ntis, m P. of colo, one who reveres: religionum colentes, religious men.

coliphia.definition: cōlīphia (coll-, cōlȳ-) ōrum, n, kwlu/fia, flesh-cakes (food for athletes), Iu.

collis.definition: 'collis is, m 2 CEL-, an elevation, high ground, hill: iugum collis, Cs.: aequaliter declivis, Cs.: leniter adclivis, Cs.: altus, O.: celsus, V.: septem colles, i. e. Rome, H.: summa collium insederant, Ta.'

collum.definition: collum ī, n the neck: in collum invasit, fell upon the neck: collo dare bracchia circum, V.: maternum, O.: complecti lacertis, O.: poenam collo sustinere: colla fovet, i. e. rests, V.: in laqueum inserere: laqueo pres…

collybus.definition: collybus ī, m, ko/llubos, exchange, agio.— The rate of exchange.

collyrium.definition: collȳrium ī, n, kollu/rion, a liquid eye-salve. —Plur., H., Iu.

colo.definition: colō coluī, cultus, ere COL-, to till, tend, care for, cultivate: agrum, T.: agros, Cs.: colendi causā in agro esse: agri qui coluntur: hortos, V.: arbores, H.: fructūs, V.: fruges, O.: Pater ipse colendi, V.—To frequ…

colocasium.definition: colocāsium ī, n, koloka/sion, an Egyptian bean, marsh-lily, V.

colona.definition: colōna ae, f colonus, a countrywoman, O.

colonia.definition: colōnia ae, f colonus, a colony, colonial town, settlement: incolumis: in colonias mittere, L.: colonias constituere: in colonias deduci.— Persons sent out for settlement, a colony, colonists, planters: coloniam deduc…

colonicus.definition: colōnicus adj. colonus, colonial: cohortes, i. e. levied from colonies, Cs.

colonus.definition: colōnus ī, m COL-, a husbandman, tiller of the soil: optimus, parcissimus: Pauper ruris, H.: mandere vestros colonos, i. e. oxen, O.—A farmer, peasant: navīs suis colonis implere, Cs.: qui colonus habuit conductum fun…

color.definition: color (old colōs, S., L.), ōris, m 2 CAL-, color, hue, tint: nivis, O.: caeruleus, Cs.: Tyrios mirare, H.: flores mille colorum, O.: color in pomo est ater, O.: varios mentiri colores, V.: scuta lectissimis coloribus …

coloratus.definition: colōrātus adj. P. of coloro, colored: arcus. —Swarthy, dusky: Indi, V.: voltus, Ta.

coloro.definition: colōrō āvī, ātus, āre color, to give a color to, color, tinge, dye: corpora.—Fig., of style: orationem illorum (librorum) tactu quasi colorari.

colossus.definition: colossus ī, m, kolosso/s, a gigantio statue, colossus, Iu.

coluber.definition: coluber brī, m 1 CEL-, a serpent, snake, V.; of the Hydra, O.; of Medusa, O.; of Allecto, V.

colubra.definition: colubra ae, f coluber, a female serpent, serpent, snake, H., O., Iu.— Of the hair of the furies, O.; of Medusa, O.

colubrifer.definition: 'colubrifer fera, ferum, adj. coluber + FER-, serpent-bearing: monstrum (i. e. Medusa), O.'

colum.definition: cōlum ī, n a vessel for straining, colander, V.

columba.definition: 'columba ae, f 2 CAL-, a dove, pigeon, C.: volucris, V., H., O.: Cythereiades (as sacred to Venus), O.'

columbinus.definition: columbīnus columba, of a dove, of a pigeon: pulli: ovum, H.

columbus.definition: columbus ī, m 2 CAL-, a male dove, cockpigeon, Ct., H.

columella.definition: 'columella ae, f dim. columna, a small column, pillar, C.: pedum in altitudinem quinque, Cs.'

columen.definition: columen inis, n 2 CEL-, a pillar, column: fax, quae magnum ad columen volabat, like an ascending column: excelsum, a pedestal: Phrygiae columina (of mountains), Ct. — Fig., of persons, the crown, summit, first, chief:…

columna.definition: columna ae, f 2 CEL-, a column, pillar, post: columnam efficere: columnae templa sustinent: ad perpendiculum columnas exigere. — Poet.: ne pede proruas Stantem columnam, i. e. destroy the city, H.—Esp.. Columna Maenia…

columnarium.definition: columnārium ī, n columna, a duty on pillars in buildings, pillar-tax, Cs., C.

colurnus.definition: 'colurnus adj. for * corulnus, from corylus, of the hazel, of hazel-wood: verna, V.'

colus.definition: colus (ūs or ī), abl. colō or colū, f (m Ct., Pr.), a distaff: tua, V., O., Iu.

com-.definition: com- praep., old form of 1 cum.

coma.definition: coma ae, f, ko/mh, the hair of the head, hair: calamistrata: flava, H.: intonsa, V.: deciderint comae, H.: compositae, O.: comas religata, H.: positu variare, O.: scissa comam, V.: laniata comas, O.: aurea, the golden…

comans.definition: comāns antis, adj. P. of comō, āre, from coma, hairy, long - haired, covered with hair: colla equorum, V.: saetae hircorum, bristling hair, V.: galea (i. e. cristata), plumed, V. — Hairy, leafy: stella, a comet, O.: s…

comata.definition: comāta ae, adj. f coma, long-haired: Gallia, Transalpine Gaul: silva, in leaf, Ct.

combibo1.definition: com-bibō (con-b-) bibī, —, ere, to drink up, absorb, imbibe: combibunt guttura sucos, O.: venenum corpore, H.—To repress, conceal: lacrimas meas, O.—To absorb, take up, swallow, engulf: ara cruorem Conbiberat, O.: Com…

combibo2.definition: combibō (conb-) ōnis, m a pot - companion.

comburo.definition: combūrō (conb-) ūssī, ūstus, ere PVR-, to burn up, consume: subsellia: navīs, Cs.: legatum vivum: puerum.—Fig., to ruin: alqm iudicio.

comedo.definition: com-edō ēdī, ēsus or ēstus, ēsse or edere, to eat up, eat, consume, devour: quid comedent? T.: (venenum) comestum: haec porcis comedenda relinques, H.—To waste, dissipate, spend, squander: nummos: patrimonium: nobilit…

comes.definition: comes itis, m and f com- + 1 I-, a companion, associate, comrade, partaker, sharer, partner. omnino sine comite venisse, quite alone: Comites secuti sunt virginem, T.: eius Rubrius: o socii comitesque, H.: cui fides A…

cometes.definition: comētēs ae, m, komh/ths, a comet, C., V.: sidus cometes, Ta.

comice.definition: cōmicē adv. comicus, in the manner of comedy: res tragicas tractare.

comicus.definition: cōmicus adj., kwmiko/s, of comedy, comic, in comic style: poëta: artificium: res, the material of comedy, H. — Represented in comedy: senes: adulescens.—As subst m., a comic poet, writer of comedy.

comis.definition: cōmis e, adj. with comp, courteous, affable, kind, obliging, friendly, loving: homines: illo usa sum benigno et comi, T.: quis Laelio comior?: conviva, H.: bonis, Ta.: erga aliquem: in uxorem, H.: comi hospitio, L.: v…

comissabundus.definition: 'comissabundus adj. comissor, revelling, riotously: incessit, L.: exercitus, Cu.'

comissatio.definition: cōmissātiō (cōmess-) ōnis, f comissor, a Bacchanalian revel, revelry, C., L.

comissator.definition: cōmissātor (cōmess-) ōris, m comissor, a reveller, rioter: haud commodus, T.: comissatorum conspectus: commissatores coniurationis.

comissor.definition: cōmissor (comm-) ātus, ārī, dep., kwma/zw, to revel, make merry, hold carnival: ad fratrem, L.: in domum alicuius, H.: comissantium curru, of revellers, L.—Supin. acc.: Phaedriam intromittamus comissatum, T.

comitas.definition: cōmitās ātis, f comis, courtesy, kindness, friendliness, affability, gentleness: illius: comitate condīta gravitas: invitandi, L.: curandi, Ta.

comitatus1.definition: comitātus adj. with comp. P. of comito, attended, escorted, accompanied: parum, with few attendants: bene: puero ut uno esset comitatior, that his train was increased by, etc.

comitatus2.definition: comitātus ūs, m comitor, an escort, train, retinue, suite: delicatus ancillarum: proficisci cum magno comitatu: praedonis: equitum: gradū s ipse comitatus habet, Ta.: Irae Insidiaeque dei comitatus, V.—Fig.: quid tant…

comiter.definition: cōmiter adv., courteously, affably, kindly: me adiuvare, T.: qui erranti comiter monstrat viam: munera missa legatis, L.: excipitur, O.: invitare iuvenes, L.: maiestatem populi R. comiter conservanto, with due courtes…

comitia.definition: comitia ōrum, n plur. of comitium, the Roman people in assembly, comitia curiata, of the patricians, held in the comitium, mainly to ratify or veto decrees of the senate: comitia fierent regi creando, L.; later only f…

comitialis.definition: comitiālis e, adj. comitia, of an election, proper for comitia: dies, L.: biduum, Cs.: mensis.

comitiatus.definition: comitiātus ūs, m comitia, an assembly of the people in the comitia: maximus: inutiles.

comitium.definition: comitium ī, n com- + I-, a place of assembly, place of meeting: in comitio esse Spartae, i. e. the Ephoreium, N.—Esp., a place adjoining the Forum, in which the Comitia curiata were held, the comitium, C., Cs., L., Ta…

comito.definition: comitō āvī, ātus, āre comes, to accompany, attend, follow: nostros gradūs, O.: vestigia, O.— P. pass.: (mulier) viris: Achate, V.: uno aut altero amicorum, Ta.

comitor.definition: comitor ātus, ārī comes, to join as an attendant, accompany, attend, follow: eos, Cs.: hostiam, V.: iter alicuius, V.: gressum, V.: lanigerae comitantur oves, V.: magnā comitante catervā, with, V.: intravit paucis com…

commaculo.definition: com-maculō āvī, ātus, āre, to spot, stain, pollute, defile: sanguine manūs, V.—Fig., to disgrace, stain: se ambitu: se cum Iugurthā miscendo, S.

commanipularis.definition: com-manipulāris is, m a soldier of the same maniple, brother in arms, Ta.

commeatus.definition: commeātus (conm-) ūs, m commeo, a going to and fro, passing back and forth: duobus commeatibus exercitum reportare, i. e. in two trips, Cs.— A leave of absence, furlough: totius aestatis: sumere, L.: in commeatu esse,…

commemini.definition: com-meminī (conm-) isse, defect, to recollect clearly, remember well: hominem: sic, T.: me miserum (fuisse): Hac, si commemini, die, O.

commemorabilis.definition: commemorābilis (conm-) e, adj. commemoro, worth mentioning, memorable: pietas.

commemorandus.definition: 'commemorandus adj. P. of commemoro, memorable: iudicia.'

commemoratio.definition: commemorātiō (conm-) ōnis, f commemoro, a reminding, commemorating, remembrance, mentioning: istaec, T.: nominis nostri: fortitudinis: adsidua flagitiorum: sua: posteritatis, by posterity.

commemoro.definition: com-memorō (conm-) āvī, ātus, āre, to recall to memory, call to mind, be mindful of, keep in mind, remember: quid dixerim. — To bring to mind, remind of, recall: quid commemorem primum? T.: ea (facta), S.: ad commemor…

commendabilis.definition: commendābilis e, adj. commendo, worthy of praise, commendable: merito, L.: apud Africa num, L.

commendaticius.definition: commendātīcius (not -tītius), adj. commen do, commendatory: litterae, letters of recommen dation, an introduction: tabellae.

commendatio.definition: commendātiō ōnis, f commendo, a commit ting, commending, recommending, recommendation: mea: tua fides fiduciam commendationi meae tribuit, i. e. to the trust I commit to you, S.: ad ceteros. — Fig.: si commendatione o…

commendatrix.definition: commendātrīx īcis, f commendo, that which commends: lex virtutum.

commendatus.definition: commendātus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of commendo, commended, recommended, acceptable, approved: cui civitas sit huius studio commendatior: a me commendatissimi.

commendo.definition: commendō (conm-) āvī, ātus, āre com- + 1 mando, to commit for protection, intrust, confide, deposit with: Oratorem meum Sabino. — Fig., to intrust, commit, confide: me tuae fidei, T.: historiam immortalitati: vita mon…

commentariolum.definition: commentāriolum ī, n dim. commentarius, a short treatise, brief commentary.

commentarius.definition: commentārius ī, m (sc. liber), or commentarium, ī, n (sc. volumen) commentor, a notebook, notes, memorandum: recita commentarium: quod de apparatibus belli fecerat, L.—Plur, memoirs, records: quos scripsit (Caesar) re…

commentatio.definition: commentātiō ōnis, f commentor, a diligent meditation, study, careful preparation: mortis: ferendi doloris.—Plur: accuratae ac meditatae.

commentatus.definition: commentātus adj. P. of 1 commentor, thought out; neut. plur. as subst, mental compositions: sua.

commenticius.definition: commentīcius (not -tītius), adj. comminiscor, thought out, devised, fabricated, invented, new: nomina.—Feigned, pretended, ideal, imaginary: civitas Platonis: di: crimen, false.

commentor1.definition: commentor ātus, ārī, intens. comminiscor, to meditate, think over, study, deliberate, weigh, prepare (mentally): commentandi causā convenire, deliberation: aliquid: causam: futuras mecum miserias: de populi R. liberta…

commentor2.definition: commentor ōris, m com- + 1 MAN-, a deviser, discoverer: uvae, i. e. Bacchus, O.

commentum.definition: commentum ī, n comminiscor, an invention, fabrication, pretence, fiction, falsehood: ipsis commentum placet, T.: opinionum commenta delet dies; miraculi, L.: milia rumorum, O.

commentus.definition: 'commentus adj. P. of comminiscor, devised, invented, feigned, fictitious: funera, O.: crimen, L.'

commeo.definition: com-meō (conm-) āvī, ātus, āre, to go and come, pass to and fro, move back and forth, go about: ultro citro: tuto ab hostium incursu, Cs.: quā viā omnes commeabant, N.: illo mari, Ta.: ad ea furta quae reliquisses.—To…

commercium.definition: commercium (conm-) ī, n com- + merx, commercial intercourse, trade, traffic, commerce: mare et lingua commercia prohibebant, S.: portūs per commercia cogniti, Ta.: legati prohibiti commercio, L. — The right to trade, …

commercor.definition: com-mercor (conm-) ātus, ārī, dep., to buy up, purchase: arma, tela, S.

commereo.definition: com-mereō (conm-) uī, itus, ēre, to merit fully, deserve, incur, earn: aliquam aestimationem: ut caperet odium illam mei, T.: poenam, O.— To commit, be guilty of, perpetrate: culpam, T.: alqd, T., O.

commereor.definition: com-mereor (conm-) itus sum, ērī, dep., to commit, be guilty of: numquam quicquam erga me, T.

commetior.definition: com-mētior (conm-) mēnsus, īrī, dep., to measure: siderum ambitūs inter se numero. — Fig., to measure, proportion: negotium cum tempore.

commeto.definition: commētō (conm-) —, —, āre, freq. commeo, to visit habitually: ad mulierculam, T.

commigro.definition: com-migrō (conm-) āvī, ātus, āre, to remove, migrate, enter: huc habitatum, T.: huc viciniae, T.: in tuam (domum): Romam, L.: e Germaniā in Gallias, Ta.

commilitium.definition: commīlitium ī, n com- + militia, a campaigning together, comradeship: in commilitium asciscere, Ta.—Fig., fellowship, O.

commilito.definition: com-mīlitō ōnis, m a comrade, fellow-soldier, C.: commilitones adpellans, Cs., L.

comminatio.definition: comminātiō ōnis, f comminor, a threatening, menacing: orationis tamquam armorum. — Plur: Hannibalis, L.

commingo.definition: com-mingō minxī, mictus (minctus), ere, to pollute, defile: lectum potus, H.: commicta lupa, Ct.: suavia salivā, Ct.

comminiscor.definition: com-minīscor (conm-) mentus, ī, dep. 1 MAN-, to devise, invent, contrive: nihil adversus tale alqd, L.: vectigal, L. — To devise falsely, contrive, invent, feign: alquid, T.: nec me hoc commentum putes: deos nihil age…

comminor.definition: com-minor (conm-) ātus, ārī, dep., to threaten, menace: pugnam, L.: inter se, L.

comminuo.definition: com-minuō (conm-) uī, ūtus, ere, to divide into small parts, break, crumble, crush, split: scalas, S.: anulum. — To lessen, diminish: argenti pondus, H.: opes civitatis. — Fig., to weaken, impair, violate: officium.— …

comminus.definition: comminus (not cōminus), adv. com- + manus, in close contest, hand to hand, at close quarters: acriter instare, S.: eminus hastis aut comminus gladiis uti: unum ense ferit, O.: comminus eminus petunt, L.: locus pugnand…

commisceo.definition: com-misceō (conm-) miscuī, mīxtus (mīstus), ē re, to mix, mingle together, intermingle: ignem cum urbis incendio: frusta commixta mero, V.: Chio nota si commixta Falerni est, H.: fumus in auras Commixtus, V.— Fig., to…

commiseratio.definition: commiserātiō ōnis, f commiseror. — In rhet., an appeal to compassion, C., Her.

commiseresco.definition: com - miserēscō (conm-) —, —, ere, inch, to commiserate, have sympathy with. — Impers.: ipsam Bacchidem eius commiseresceret, even Bacchis would pity him, T.

commiseror.definition: com-miseror (conm-) ātus, ārī, dep., to commiserate, pity, bewail: fortunam Graeciae, N.: cum commiserari coeperit, to appeal for pity.

commissio.definition: commissiō ōnis, f committo, a beginning of a contest, onset: ab ipsā commissione persequi.

commissum.definition: commissum ī, n committo, an undertaking, enterprise: audacter commissum corrigere, L.—A transgression, offence, fault, crime: sacrum: turpe, H.: commissi praemia, O.: poenā commissa luere, offences, V.—A secret, trust…

commissura.definition: commissūra ae, f committo, a joining together, joint, seam, juncture, commissure: molles digitorum: mirabiles ossium: pluteorum, Cs.

commitigo.definition: com-mītigō (conm-) —, —, āre, to make soft, mellow: tibi sandalio caput, T.

committo.definition: com - mittō (conm-) mīsī, missus, ere. I. To bring together, join, combine, put together, connect, unite: commissis operibus, L.: fidibusque commissa Moenia, O.: domus plumbo commissa, patched, In.: commissa inter se …

commode.definition: commodē adv. with comp. and sup. commodus, duly, properly, completely, rightly, well, skilfully, neatly: saltare, N.: multa dicta: cogitare, T.: non minus commode, just as well, Cs.: commodius fecissent, si, etc. — Co…

commoditas.definition: commoditās ātis, f commodus, fitness, convenience, a fit occasion, advantage, benefit: si corrigitur, quot commoditates vide, T.: ad faciendum idonea: maximas commoditates amicitia continet: cum commoditas iuvaret, L.…

commodo.definition: commodō āvī, ātus, āre commodus, to serve with, accommodate, grant, supply, lend: alqd illi, T.: quicquid possit commodari: testī s falsos, to furnish, S.: nomen suum alicui: suas vires, aliis eas commodando, minuere,…

commodum1.definition: commodum ī, n commodus, a convenient opportunity, favorable condition, convenience: meum: cum erit tuum, when it shall be convenient for you: spatium ad dicendum nostro commodo habere, at our convenience: quas (navīs)…

commodum2.definition: 'commodum adv. commodus, just, just then, just now (colloq.): commodum Enim egeram diligentissime, had just been arguing: id cum hoc agebam commodum, was just talking of, T.: commodum discesseras, cum Trebatius venit:…

commodus.definition: commodus adj. with comp. and sup. cum- + modus, with due measure, full, complete, of full weight: cyathis commodis miscentur pocula, H.— Of things, suitable, fit, convenient, opportune, commodious, easy, appropriate, …

commolior.definition: com-mōlior (conm-) ītus, īrī, dep., to set in motion, wield: dolum, Caecil. ap. C.

commonefacio.definition: commone-faciō (conm-) fēcī, factus, pass. -fīō , -factus, -faciendus, -fierī commoneo + facio, to recall, bring to mind: istius turpem praeturam. — To remind, put in mind, admonish, impress upon: te propter magnitudin…

commoneo.definition: com-moneō (conm-) uī, itus, ēre, to remind, put in mind, impress upon, bring to recollection: ut commoneri nos satis sit: quod vos lex commonet: de avaritiā tuā commoneri: quam id mihi sit facile, exempla commonent, T.

commonstro.definition: com - mōnstrō (conm-) āvī, ātus, āre, to show, point out distinctly: parentīs mihi, T.: commonstrarier Mi istum volo, T.: aurum alicui: viam.

commoratio.definition: commorātiō ōnis, f commoror, a tarrying, lingering, sojourning.— In rhet., a dwelling on.

commoror.definition: com-moror (conm-) ātus, ārī, dep., to tarry, linger, abide, sojourn, remain, stay: illic tam diu, T.: dies XXV in eo loco, Cs.: Romae: apud alqm: commorandi natura devorsorium nobis dedit: paululum, S.—Of discourse, t…

commotio.definition: commōtiō ōnis, f commoveo, a rousing, excitement, agitation, commotion: suavis iucunditatis in corpore: animorum: temperantia moderatrix commotionum, of the passions.

commotiuncula.definition: commōtiuncula ae, f dim. commotio, a little disturbance, slight indisposition.

commotus.definition: commōtus adj. with comp. P. of commoveō, moved, excited, aroused: genus (dicendi) in agendo: animus commotior: commotius ad omnia turbanda consilium, L.

commoveo.definition: com-moveō (conm-) mōvī (commōrat, T.; commōrit, H.; commōssem, commōsset, commōsse, C.), mōtus, ēre. I. To put in violent motion, move, shake, stir: alas, V.: quis sese commovere potest? can stir: commovere se non sun…

commune.definition: commūne is, n communis, that which is common: ut communibus pro communibus utatur: communia laudas, publicity, H.: sed ne communia solus occupet, the sole credit for common achievements, O.: ius statuere communi divid…

communicatio.definition: commūnicātiō ōnis, f communico, a making common, imparting, communicating: civitatis: utilitatum.—In rhet., a consultation of the hearers.

communico.definition: commūnicō (conm-) āvī, ātus, āre communis, to divide with, communicate, impart, share: alqd cum proximis: vobiscum praemia laudis: civitatem nostram vobiscum, L.: causam civium cum servis, S.: At sua Tydides mecum com…

communicor.definition: (commūnicor) ātus, ārī, dep. for communico, to impart, share: cum alquibus spem, L.

communio1.definition: com-mūniō (conm-) īvī (īvīsti or ī stī), ītus, īre, to fortify on all sides, secure, barricade, intrench: castella, Cs.: castra, L.: suos locos, S.: loca castellis idonea, N. — Fig., to make sure, strengthem: testimon…

communio2.definition: commūniō ōnis, f communis, a community, mutual participation, fellowship: inter alquos legis: sanguinis: litterarum: parietum, Ta.

communis.definition: commūnis (conm-) e, adj. with comp. MV-, common, general, universal, public: omnia inter eos: communīs natos habent, offspring in common, V.: unum et commune periclum Ambobus erit, V.: paries domui communis utrique, O…

communitas.definition: commūnitās ātis, f communis, community, society, fellowship, friendly intercourse: nulla cum deo homini: deorum et hominum: virtutes quae in communitate cernuntur. — Courtesy, condescension, affability, N.

communiter.definition: commūniter adv. communis, together, in common, jointly, generally: omnia cum Chrysogono possidet: ira urit utrumque, H.: haec omnia communiter cum conlegā (sc. facta sunt).

communitio.definition: commūnītiō ōnis, f 1 communio.—Prop., road-making; hence, in rhet., an approach.

commurmuror.definition: com-murmuror ātus, ārī, dep., to murmur in company: secum ipse.

commutabilis.definition: commūtābilis (conm-) e, adj. commuto, subject to change, changeable: cera: commutabilis, varius, multiplex animus: ratio vitae.—In rhet.: exordium, appropriate to either party.

commutatio.definition: commūtātiō (conm-) ōnis, f commuto, a changing, change, alteration: tempestatum atque caeli: temporum: magnae rerum, Cs.: tanta, S.

commuto.definition: com-mūtō (conm-) āvī, ātus, āre, to alter wholly, change entirely: signa rerum: quae commutantur fiuntque contraria: leges. — Fig.: ad commutandos animos.—To change, exchange, interchange, replace, substitute, barter,…

como1.definition: cōmō cōmpsī (msī), cōmptus, ere com- + emo, to comb, arrange, braid, dress: compti capilli: crines, Tb.: caput, Tb. — To adorn, array, deck: sacerdos comptus olivā, wreathed, V.: pueri compti, H.

comoedia.definition: cōmoedia ae, f, kwmw|di/a, a comedy: comoediam facere, T.: agere, T.: scribere: antiqua: vetus, H.

comoedus.definition: cōmoedus adj., kwmw|do/s, of comedy, comic: natio, given to acting, Iu.—As subst m., a comedian, comic actor, C., Iu.

comosus.definition: comōsus adj. coma, with long hair: frons, Ph.

compactio.definition: compāctiō ōnis, f compingo, a joining together: membrorum.

compactum.definition: (compactum, or conpectum, ī) n com- + paciscor, an agreement, only abl sing.: compacto, according to agreement, by concert: conpecto res acta, L.

compages.definition: compāgēs (conp-) is, f com- + PAC-, a joining together, joint, structure: Efficere lapidum conpagibus arcum, O.: laxae laterum, V.: artae, V.: compagibus aquam accipere (of a ship), L.: scutorum, Ta.—Fig.: in his comp…

compago.definition: compāgō inis, f rare for compages, a joining, joint, fastening: cerae, O.: fixa tabernae, Iu.

compar.definition: com-pār (conp-) paris, adj. (abl. ī; poet. also e), like, equal to, corresponding: consilium consilio, L.: tribuni tribunis compares, L.: conubium, L.: compari Marte concurrerat, L. — As subst m., a yokefellow, mate, …

comparabilis.definition: comparābilis (conp-) e, adj. 2 comparo, to be compared, comparable: species: mors trium virorum, L.

comparate.definition: comparātē adv. 2 comparo, by comparison, comparatively: quaerere.

comparatio1.definition: comparātiō (conp-) ōnis, f 1 comparo, a preparing, providing for, preparation: novi belli: veneni, L.: dicendi.—A procuring, gaining, acquiring: testium: voluptatis: criminis, i. e. of the materials for an accusation.

comparatio2.definition: comparātiō (conp-) ōnis, f 2 comparo, a comparing, comparison, inquiry by comparison: de duobus honestis utrum honestius: alqd in comparationem referre, to challenge comparison, Ta.— A relation, aspect: eadem inter se…

comparativus.definition: comparātīvus adj. 2 comparo, of comparison, comparative: iudicatio.

compareo.definition: com-pāreō (conp-) uī, —, ēre, to be evident, appear, be plain, be visible: vestigia, quibus exitūs eorum compareant: ut a naturā incohata compareant, may be seen.—To be present, be at hand, exist: signa et dona omnia:…

comparo1.definition: com-parō (conp-) āvī, ātus, āre, to prepare, make ready, set in order, furnish, provide: ad magnitudinem frigorum sibi remedium: se, to get ready: se ad iter, L.: se ad omnīs casūs, Cs.: insidias Habito: dolum ad capi…

comparo2.definition: comparō (conp-) āvī, ātum, āre compar, to bring together as equals, connect, pair, match, unite, join: donum dono contra, to set in opposition, T.: ea inter se: priore consulatu inter se conparati, L. — To bring toget…

compasco.definition: com-pāscō (con-) —, ere, to feed together, feed in common: ius est compascere.

compascuus.definition: com-pāscuus adj., of common pasturage, common: ager.

compellatio.definition: compellātiō ōnis, f 2 compello, an accosting, Her.— A reprimand, reproof.

compello1.definition: com - pellō (conp-) pulī, pulsus, ere, to drive together, drive in a body, collect, assemble: armentum in speluncam, L.: greges in unum, V.: pecus totius provinciae: (navīs) in portum, Cs.: adversarios intra moenia, N…

compello2.definition: compellō (conp-) āvī, ātus, āre 1 compello, to accost, address: alqm voce, V.: Hersiliam iussis vocibus: Tauream nomine, L.: Danaum verbis amicis, V. — To address reproachfully, reproach, chide, rebuke, upbraid, abuse…

compendiarius.definition: compendiārius (conp-) adj. compendium, short, easy: via ad gloriam.

compendium.definition: compendium (conp-) ī, n com- + pendo, gain, profit: alquem cum compendio dimittere: in quaestu compendioque versati: compendii sui causā: suo privato compendio servire, Cs.: privatum conpendium (eos) in hostem acuebat…

compensatio.definition: compēnsātiō (conp-) ōnis, f compenso, a recompense, equivalent, compensation: hac uti conpensatione ut, etc.

compenso.definition: com-pēnsō (conp-) āvī, ātus, āre, to balance, make good, compensate, counterbalance: cum uno versiculo tot volumina laudum: laetitiam cum doloribus: bona cum vitiis, H.: damna ab isto aetatis fructu compensata, made u…

comperco.definition: compercō (-parcō) persī, —, ere com- + parco, to save, hoard, lay up: alqd, T.

comperendinatus.definition: comperendinātus ūs, m (C.), and comperendinātiō , ōnis, f (Ta.) comperendino, in law, an adjournment over one entire judicial day (required by law after pleading and before judgment).

comperendino.definition: comperendinō āvī, ātus, āre com- + perendinus, to adjourn over an entire day, cite for the third judicial day: istum comperendinatum iudicare, i. e. awaiting judgment: ut ante primos ludos comperendinem, i. e. reach t…

comperio.definition: comperiō perī, pertus, īre 1 PAR-, to obtain knowledge of, find out, ascertain, learn: certo, T.: nihil de hoc: de scelere filii, N.: aliquid ex multis: nihil testibus, nihil tabulis: ut postea ex captivis comperit, C…

comperior.definition: comperior (conp-) pertus sum, īrī, dep. for comperio, to ascertain, learn, find out: ab hoc me falli, T.: Metellum sapientem virum fuisse, S.

compertus.definition: compertus adj. P. of comperio, ascertained, clearly known: quod de his duobus habuerint compertum: nobis ea res parum comperta est, S.— As subst n.: de his haud facile conpertum narraverim, exact information, S.

compes.definition: (compēs or con-pēs, pedis) f a fetter, shackle (for the feet; usu. plur.): habendae compedes, must be worn, T.: ille ex compedibus: compedibus vincire alqm, Iu. — Sing. (only abl.): durā, H.: magnā, Iu.—Fig., fetters,…

compesco.definition: compescō pescuī, —, ere PARC-, to confine, hold in check, repress, curb, restrain: equum freno, Tb.: ramos fluentes, i. e. to prune, V.: bracchia, O.: mare, H.—Fig., to suppress, repress, restrain, check, subdue: siti…

competitor.definition: competītor ōris, m competo, a rival, opposing candidate, competitor: a quo es victus: inter dimicantes competitores, L.

competitrix.definition: competītrīx īcis, f competitor, a female competitor: scaena, a display of games by a rival candidate.

competo.definition: com - petō (conp-) —, —, ere, to coincide with, happen at the same time: tempora cum exitu Othonis, Ta.—To be adequate, be suitable, be fit: ad arma capienda, L.: neque oculis neque auribus, Ta.

compilatio.definition: compīlātiō ōnis, f compilo, a pillaging, plundering; sportively of a collection of documents, a compilation: Chresti.

compilo.definition: compīlō āvī, ātus, āre, to plunder, pillage, rifle, rob: fana: si malui compilari quam venire: hortos: te, H.: Crispini scrinia, H.: ipsum (Iovem), Ph.: ab iure consultis sapientiam, steal.

compingo.definition: compingō (conp-) pēgī, pāctus, ere com- + pango, to join together, frame, make by joining; only P. perf.: septem compacta cicutis Fistula, V.: harundinibus compacta fistula, O.—Fig., of the Stoic philos.: tam composit…

compitalia.definition: compitālia iōrum compitum, n a festival in honor of the Lares.

compitalicius.definition: compitālicius adj. compitalia, of the Compitalia: ludi: dies.

compitum.definition: compitum ī, n 1 PAT-, a crossing of roads, place where roads cross: Anagninum. — Plur, a cross-way, cross-roads, corner, L.: in compitis auctionari: frequentia, H.

complaceo.definition: (com-placeō) placitus, ēre, to please greatly: tibi, T.

complano.definition: com-plānō —, ātus, āre, to level, make even, raze: domum.

complector.definition: complector or conplector plexus, ī, dep. PARC-, PLEC-, to clasp, embrace, grasp: mulierem, T.: patrem: nepotes, V.: dextram euntis, V.: pedes, V.: membra lacertis, O.: inter nos: inter se, L.: Te comitem, V. — To gras…

complementum.definition: complēmentum ī, n compleo, that which fills up, a complement: numerorum (inania quaedam verba): accusationum, that gives them full weight, Ta.

compleo.definition: compleō or conpleō ēvī (complērunt, complē sse), ētus, ēre com- + PLE-, to fill up, fill full, fill out, make full, cram, crowd: hostes fossam complent, Cs.: cum sanguis os oculosque complesset: metu, ne compleantur n…

completus.definition: complētus adj. P. of compleo, complete, perfect: verborum ambitus.

complexio.definition: complexiō (conp-) ōnis, f PARC-, PLEC-, a combination, association: cumulata bonorum.— Of discourse, a summing up, comprehension: brevis totius negotii.—A sentence, period, expression: mira verborum.—In philosophy, a …

complexus2.definition: complexus (con-) ūs, m PARC-, PLEC-, a surrounding, encompassing, encircling, embracing, embrace, clasp, grasp: (mundus) omnia complexu suo continet: alqm de complexu parentum rapere: divelli a parentum complexu, S.: …

complico.definition: com-plicō (conp-) āvī, ātus, āre, to fold together, fold up: epistulam.—Fig., to fold, roll up: animi complicata notio, involved.

comploratio.definition: complōrātiō (conp-) ōnis, f comploro, a loud complaint, concerted wailing, lamentation: lamentabilis mulierum, L.: sororis, L.: sui patriaeque, bewailing, L.

comploratus.definition: complōrātus (conp-) ūs, m comploro, a loud moaning, concerted wailing, lamentation: familiarum, L.: conploratu prosequi mortuos, L.

comploro.definition: com-plōrō (conp-) āvī, ātus, āre, to bewail, lament loudly: penates, O.: mortui complorarentur, L.: morte comploratā: complorata res est p., despaired of, L.

complures.definition: com-plūrēs (conp-) a or ia; gen. ium, adj., more than one, not a few, several, a number, many: scriptores ante nos, N.: mulieres, T.: boni, S.: scyphorum paria: loca, L.: Complurīs alios praetereo, H.: ratibus complur…

complusculi.definition: complūsculī (conp-) ae, a, adj. dim. complures, a good many, not a few: dies, T.

compono.definition: com-pōnō (conp-) posuī (-posīvī, Ta.), positus (-postus, V.), ere, to bring together, place together, collect, unite, join, connect, aggregate: in quo loco erant ea composita, quibus, etc.: aridum lignum, H.: duos ama…

comporto.definition: com-portō (conp-) āvī, ātus, āre, to bring in, carry together, collect, accumulate, gather: argentum ad se: eo frumentum ex Asiā , Cs.: arma in templum: ad aggerem caespitibus conportandis, Cs.: aurum domum regiam, S.…

compos.definition: com-pos (conp-) potis, adj. com- + POT-, master of, powerful over, possessing, participating in: animi, sane, T.: mentis: sui, L.: rationis et consili: eius doni, sharing in, L.: huius urbis: me conpotem voti facere, …

composite.definition: compositē (conp-) adv with comp. compono, in an orderly manner, orderly, regularly, properly: dicere: casum rei p. miserati, S.: compositius cuncta agere, with deliberation, Ta.

compositio.definition: compositiō (conp-) ōnis, f compono, a putting together, connecting, arranging, composition: unguentorum: membrorum: anni, of the calendar—A matching: gladiatorum.—Fig., connection, coherence, system disciplinae.—A dra…

composito.definition: compositō (conp-) adv. P. abl. of compono, by agreement, by conspiracy, by preconcert: Composito factum est, quo modo, etc., T.: composito fecisse, ut, etc, N.: rumpit vocem, as had been arranged, V.

compositor.definition: compositor (conp-) ōris, m compono, a maker, composer compositor aut actor (of discourse): operum, O.

compositum.definition: compositum (conp-) ī, n compono, an agreement, compact: ex composito orta vis, L., Cu.

compositus.definition: compositus (conp-, -postus) adj. with comp. and sup. P. of compono, well - ordered, orderly, regular: Nec magis compositum quicquam, T.: acrior impetu quam compositior ullo ordine pugna fuit, L.: litterulae compositis…

compotatio.definition: com-pōtātiō ōnis, f a drinking together.

compotrix.definition: com-pōtrīx īcis, f a drinking-companion, T.

compransor.definition: com-prānsor ōris, m a boon companion.

comprecatio.definition: comprecātiō ōnis, f comprecor, a general supplication: sollemnis deorum, L.

comprecor.definition: com-precor (conp-) ātus, ārī, dep., to pray to, supplicate, implore: deos, T.: caelestūm fidem, Ct.: Cythereïa, comprecor, ausis Adsit, O.

comprehendo.definition: com-prehendō (conp-) or comprēndō, dī, sus, ere, to bind together, unite: eas navīs funibus, L.—To take hold of, seize, catch, grasp, apprehend: quid (opus est) manibus, si nihil comprehendendum est?: comprehendunt ut…

comprehensibilis.definition: comprehēnsibilis (conp-) e, adj. comprehendo, conceivable, intelligible.

comprehensio.definition: comprehēnsiō (conp-) ōnis, f comprehendo, a seizing, laying hold of: sessio, comprehensio: sontium, arrest.—Fig., a comprehension, perception: rerum. — A combining: consequentium rerum cum primis. — In rhet., a period…

compresse.definition: (compressē) adv. comprimo, briefly, succinctly; only comp. compressius loqui.

compressio.definition: compressiō (conp-) ōnis, f comprimo, concise expression, condensation: rerum.

compressus2.definition: (compressus ūs), m comprimo, a compression (only abl sing.): semen compressu suo diffindit (terra).—An embrace, T.

comprimo.definition: com-primō (conp-) pressī, pressus, ere, to press together, bring together, compress, close: (digitos) compresserat pugnumque fecerat: labra, H.: oculos (of the dead), O.: murem, Ph.: ordines (of the army), to close, L…

comprobatio.definition: comprobātiō ōnis, f comprobo, approbation, approval: honestatis.

comprobator.definition: comprobātor ōris, m comprobo, an approver.

comprobo.definition: com-probō (conp-) āvī, ātus, āre, to approve, assent to, sanction, acknowledge: sententiam: (bellum) ab omnibus comprobatur: orationem omnium adsensu, L.: alqd publice, N.—To prove, establish, attest, make good, show,…

compromissum.definition: comprōmissum ī, n compromitto, an agreement to abide by the award of an arbiter: facere: iudicium de compromisso facere.

compromitto.definition: com-prōmittō (conp-) mīsī, missus, ere, to agree to abide by the award of an arbiter.

comptus.definition: cōmptus (comt-) adj. with comp. P. of 1 como, in order, smoothed, adorned: in comptum comas religata nodum, H.: iuvenes, with hair brushed, H., O.— Fig., of style, ornate, embellished: oratio: comtior oratio, Ta.

compungo.definition: com-pungō (conp-) nxī, nctus, ere, to prick severely, sting, prod, puncture: collum dolone, Ph.: compunctus notis Threïciis, tattooed. — Fig., to prick, goad: se suis acuminibus.

computo.definition: com-putō (conp-) āvī, ātus, āre, to sum up, reckon, compute: computarat, pecuniam imperarat. —Fig., to count: facies tua computat annos, i. e. reveals, Iu.

conamen.definition: cōnāmen inis, n conor, an effort, exertion, struggle: magno conamine, O.: sumpto positā conamine ab hastā, O.: conamina mortis, attempts at suicide, O.—A support, prop: adiutis aliquo conamine nervis, O.

conata.definition: cōnāta ōrum, n 1 conatus, an undertaking, attempt, venture, hazard, plan: perficere, Cs.: Carthaginiensium, L.: peragere, Iu.

conatus2.definition: cōnātus ūs, m conor, an attempt, effort, undertaking, enterprise, endeavor: audax, L.: hoc conatu destiterunt, Cs.: princeps ad conatum exercitū s conparandi: conatum Antoni reppulerunt: de spe conatuque depulsus: com…

concaco.definition: con-cacō āvī, ātus, āre, to defile with ordure, cover with filth: totam regiam, Ph.

concaedes.definition: con-caedēs ium, f an abattis, barricade of felled trees: latera concaedibus munitus, Ta.

concalefacio.definition: con-calefaciō fēcī, factus, ere, to warm thoroughly: bracchium: (concursio corporum) concalefacta.

concalesco.definition: con-calēscō luī, —, ere, to grow hot, glow: corpora ardore animi.—Fig. (of love), T.

concallesco.definition: con - callēscō calluī, ere calleo, to grow hard: manus opere ... animus usu.—Fig., to become insensible: locus animi concalluit.

concavo.definition: concavō —, ātus, āre, to make hollow, round, curve: bracchia in arcūs, O.

concavus.definition: 'con-cavus adj., hollow, concave, arched, vaulted, bent, curved: aera, O.: altitudines speluncarum: saxa, V.: bracchia Cancri, O.'

concedo.definition: con-cēdō cessī, cessus, ere. I. Intrans, to go away, pass, give way, depart, retire, withdraw, remove: biduom, T.: tempus est concedere, T.: superis ab oris, V.: ad Manes, V.: huc, T.: istuc, T.: aliquo ab eorum oculi…

concelebro.definition: con-celebrō āvī, ātus, āre, to attend in numbers, frequent, celebrate, solemnize: funus, L.: at rem concelebrandam putavit: dapes, O. — To honor, praise: genium choreis, Tb.—To prosecute eagerly: studia per otium.—To …

concenatio.definition: con-cēnātiō (not -coen-), ōnis, f a supping together, companionship at table.

concentio.definition: concentiō ōnis, f con- + 1 CAN-, a singing together, harmony: clarissima.

concentus.definition: concentus ūs, m con- + 1 CAN-, a concert, symphony, harmony, harmonious music: concentum servare: vocis lyraeque, O.: avium, V.: concentibus aëra mulcent, O.: tubarum ac cornuum, L. — A choir, chorus of singers. — Fig…

conceptio.definition: conceptiō ōnis, f con- + CAP-, a conception, becoming pregnant. — Fig., a composing, drawing up (of formulas).

conceptus2.definition: conceptus ūs, m concipio, a conceiving, conception: hominum.

concerpo.definition: concerpō psī, —, ere com- + carpo, to tear in pieces, rend: epistulas: librum, L.

concertatio.definition: concertātiō ōnis, f concerto, a disputation, dispute, controversy: concertationum plenae disputationes: concertationis studium.

concertator.definition: concertātor ōris concerto, one who competes, a rival: Corbulonis, Ta.

concerto.definition: con-certō āvī, ātus, āre, to contend warmly, dispute zealously: alquid cum ero, T.: proelio, Cs. — To dispute, debate: cum Apolline de tripode: uno verbo.

concessio.definition: concessiō ōnis, f concedo, a granting, conceding: nostra: agrorum.— In rhet., a plea of confession and excuse.

concessus1.definition: concessus adj. P. of concedo, lawful, permitted (rare): Martem concessis animalibus placant, Ta.—Plur n. as subst: abhorrere a maiorum concessis, i. e. the liberty followed by, etc.: concessa petere, lawful objects, V…

concessus2.definition: (concessus ūs),m concedo, a concession, permission, leave; only abl sing.: Caesaris concessu, Cs.: concessu omnium.

concha.definition: concha ae, f, ko/gxh, a bivalve, shell - fish, mussel: squalentes, V.: cavae, O.: marinae, O.: viles, H. — A mussel-shell: ostrea in conchis suis, O.— Shells were used as trumpets; hence, poet., the trumpet of the Tri…

conchis.definition: conchis is, f, ko/gxos, a coarse bean, Iu.

conchyliatus.definition: conchȳliātus adj. conchylium, of a purple color, dyed purple: peristromata.

conchylium.definition: conchȳlium ī, n, kogxu/lion, a shell - fish, C.; a purple shell-fish, Ct. — Esp., an oyster: exstructa mensa conchyliis: miscere conchylia turdis, S.—Meton., purple color, purple: vestis conchylio tincta. — Plur, purp…

concido1.definition: concidō cidī, —, ere cado, to fall together, fall down, tumble, fall to earth: conclave illud concidit: urbs uno incendio: pinus bipenni, Ph.: ad terram, V.: sub onere, L.: concidere miratur arator tauros, O.—To fall …

concido2.definition: concīdō cīdī, cīsus, ere com- + caedo, to cut up, cut through, cut to pieces, ruin, destroy: nervos: navīs, L.: magnos scrobibus montīs, to break up mounds, V. — In battle, to cut to pieces, cut down, destroy, kill: m…

conciliabulum.definition: conciliābulum ī, n concilio, a place of assembly, public exchange, market-place, L., Ta.

conciliatio.definition: conciliātiō ōnis, f concilio, a connection, union, bond: generis hominum: civilis.—Fig., a conciliating, making friendly, gaining over: conciliationis causā. — In rhet., a gaining over, conciliating (of a judge or aud…

conciliator.definition: conciliātor ōris, m concilio, he who negotiates, a promoter: nuptiarum, N.: proditionis, L.

conciliatricula.definition: conciliātrīcula ae, f dim. conciliatrix, a minx of a matchmaker: blanda.

conciliatrix.definition: conciliātrīx īcis, f conciliator, one who mediates, a promoter: amicitiae.—Esp., a mediatrix, procuress: blanda.

conciliatus.definition: conciliātus adj. with comp. P. of concilio, endeared, beloved: Hamilcari, L.: sibi, Cu.: ad rem accipiendam fiat conciliatior.

concilio.definition: conciliō āvī, ātus, āre concilium, to bring together, unite, reconcile, make friendly, win over, conciliate: nos: inter nos legiones sibi pecuniā: homines inter se: homines sibi conciliari amiciores, N.: civitates ami…

concilium.definition: concilium ī, n com- + 1 CAL-, a meeting, rendezvous: Camenarum cum Egeriā, L.—A collection of people, meeting, assembly: pastorum: divinum animorum: amoena piorum, V.: ferarum, O.—An assembly for consultation, council…

concinne.definition: concinnē adv. concinnus, neatly, with rhetorical art: rogare: distributa, with sound judgment.

concinno.definition: concinnō āvī, ātus, āre concinnus, to cause, produce: quantum mali, Ph.

concinnus.definition: concinnus adj. with comp, neat, pretty, elegant, pleasing, stylish: Samos, pretty, H.: tectorium.—Of style: oratio: poëma: versus, H.—Of persons: helluo: alii concinniores: in brevitate respondendi, apt in repartee, N…

concino.definition: concinō cinuī, —, ere com- + cano, intrans, to sound in concert, sing harmoniously: concinunt tubae, L.: concinit albus olor, O.—Fig., to agree, harmonize, accord: inter se: cum alquo: concinentīs collegas audire, L.—…

concio1.definition: conciō, or concieō cīvī, citus, īre or ēre com- + cieo, to bring together, call together, collect: homines, L.: multitudinem ad se, L.: nunc concienda plebs, L.—To move violently, shake, stir up: concitus imbribus amn…

concipio.definition: concipiō cēpī, ceptus, ere com- + capio, to take hold of, take up, take in, take, receive: inde pabula terrae concipiunt, V.: concipit Iris aquas, draws up, O.: terra Concepit lacrimas, O.: praecordiis conceptam morte…

concisio.definition: concīsiō ōnis, f 2 concīdo.—In rhet., a dividing into short clauses.

concisus.definition: concīsus adj. P. of 2 concīdo, abrupt, short, concise: sententiae: Thrasymachus, in style.

concitatio.definition: concitātiō ōnis, f concito, a quickening, quick movement: remorum, L. — Fig., a violent passion: animi: animorum, L. — An agitation, sedition, tumult: plebi contra patres: multitudinis, Cs.

concitator.definition: concitātor ōris, m concito, a mover, exciter, ring - leader, agitator: cuius (contionis): turbae ac tumultūs, L.: tabernariorum.

concitatus.definition: concitātus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of concito, rapid, swift, quick: equo concitato vehitur, at full speed, N.: quam concitatissimos equos inmittere, L.: conversio caeli concitatior.—Fig., roused, excited, vehement…

concito.definition: concitō āvī, ātus, āre, freq. concio, to put in quick motion, rouse, excite, urge, drive, incite, spur, agitate, disturb: equum calcaribus, L.: equum in aliquem, N.: equos adversos, L.: navīs maximā celeritate, L.: te…

concitor.definition: concitor ōris, m concio, he who rouses, a stirrer up: belli, L.: volgi, L.

conclamatio.definition: conclāmātiō ōnis, f conclamo, a loud shout, acclamation: exercitūs, Cs.—Plur, outcries, Ta.
