conclamo.definition: con-clāmō āvī, ātus, āre, to cry out together, shout, make acclaim: ad quorum casum gaudio, L.: ‘procul este,’ Conclamat vates, V.: a me conservatam esse rem p.: occasionem amittendam non esse, Cs.: ducendum ad sedes …

conclave.definition: conclāve is (abl. vī), n com- + clavis, a room, chamber, suite, apartment: ultimis in aedibus, T.; of a sleeping-room, C.; a dining-hall, H.: pro conclavibus popinae sunt, dining-halls.

concludo.definition: conclūdō sī, sus, ere com- + claudo, to shut up, close, imprison, enclose, confine: bestias: multitudinem: me in cellam cum illā , T.: illum aliquo, T.: locum sulco, V.: Suave locus voci resonat conclusus, H.: conclus…

concluse.definition: conclūsē adv. concludo, with rhetorical finish: dicere.

conclusio.definition: conclūsiō ōnis concludo, a shutting up, shutting in, siege, blockade: diutina, Cs.: in hac conclusione, during this siege, N.—Fig., a conclusion, end: muneris. — In discourse, a conclusion, close, peroration: orationi…

conclusiuncula.definition: conclūsiuncula ae, f dim. conclusio, a captious conclusion, sophism: minutulae.

conclusum.definition: conclūsum ī, n P. n. of concludo, a conclusion (of a syllogism), inference.

concolor.definition: con - color colōris, adj., of the same color: cum fetu albo sus, V.: umerus sinister dextro, O.: populus festo, i. e. clothed in white, O.

concoquo.definition: con-coquō coxī, coctus, ere, to digest: conchas.—Fig., to endure, suffer, put up with, brook, tolerate: eius ista odia: alqm senatorem, L.—To revolve in mind, think upon, weigh, reflect upon, consider well: tibi diu c…

concordia.definition: concordia ae, f concors, an agreeing together, union, harmony, concord: concordiā parvae res crescunt, S.: civium: equites concordiā coniunctissimi: (consiliis) copulare concordiam, L.: reconciliatio concordiae: inter…

concorditer.definition: 'concorditer adv. with comp. and sup. concors, harmoniously, amicably, in harmony: exigit annos, O.: concordius bellum gerere, L.: quicum concordissime vixerat.'

concordo.definition: concordō āvī, ātus, āre concors, of persons, to agree, be united, be of one mind, harmonize: cum illā, T.—Fig., to be consistent, be in harmony, agree: cum eius iudicia opinionesque concordant: carmina nervis, O.

concors.definition: concors cordis, abl. dī, adj. with sup. com+ cor, of persons, of the same mind, united, agreeing, concordant, harmonious: Parcae, V.: animi, L.: eā gratiā, T.: cum concordissimis fratribus: secum ipse, L.: mihi coniun…

concredo.definition: con-crēdō didī, ditus, ere, to intrust, consign, commit: rem suam alicui: quibus obsessos muros, V.: alicui nugas, H.: gnatum ventis, Ct.: nobis, to make me your confidant, Pr.

concremo.definition: con - cremō āvī, ātus, āre, to burn up, consume: vivos igni, L.: domos, L.

concrepo.definition: con - crepō puī, pitus, āre, to rattle, creak, grate, sound, resound, clash: ostium concrepuit abs te, i. e. I heard your door open, T.: scabilla: multitudo armis, Cs.: concrepuere arma, clashed, L.: Aeriferae concrep…

concresco.definition: con-crēscō crēvī (concrēsse, O.), crētus, ere, to grow together, harden, condense, curdle, stiffen, congeal: Concrescunt in flumine crustae, V.: rigido rostro Ora, stiffen, O.: Gorgone conspectā , to be petrified, O.:…

concretio.definition: concrētiō ōnis, f concresco, a compacting, condensing, congealing: corporum.—Matter, substance: mortalis.

concretum.definition: concrētum ī, n concretus, hardness, solid matter: nihil concreti habere.—Hard frost, stiff frost (sc. gelu), V.

concretus.definition: concrētus adj. P. of concresco, condensed, hardened, thick, hard, stiff, curdled, congealed, clotted: nihil sit animis concretum: aër: spuma, O.: lac, V.: sanguis, O.: glacies, L.—Fig., thick, dim: lumen.—Inveterate: …

concubina.definition: concubīna ae, f CVB-, a concubine, C., Ta.

concubinus.definition: concubīnus ī, m CVB-, one who lives in concubinage, Cu., Ta., Ct.

concubitus.definition: concubitus ūs, m CVB-, a lying together, concubinage: ferarum ritu, L., C., V., H., Tb.

concubius.definition: concubius adj. CVB-, of lying in sleep.— Only in the phrase, concubiā nocte, in the first sleep, C., Ta.: movere concubiā nocte, to march early in the night, L.

conculco.definition: conculcō āvī, ātus, āre com- + calco, to tread upon, trample: virum.—Fig., to tread down, trample, abuse, despise, contemn: istum conculcandum putaverunt: huic conculcandam Italiam tradere: lauream: rem p. conculcatam…

concumbo.definition: concumbō cubuī, cubitus, ere CVB-, to lie together, lie with, cohabit, T., C., O., Iu., Pr.

concupiens.definition: con-cupiēns entis, adj., very desirous: regni, Enn. ap. C.

concupisco.definition: concupīscō cupīvī (sync. cupīstī, etc.), ītus, ere, inch. com- + cupio, to long for, be very desirous of, covet, aspire to, strive after: alqd: pecuniam: haec ad insaniam: domum aut villam, S.: tribunos plebis, L.: el…

concurro.definition: con-currō currī or cucurrī, cursus, ere, to run together, assemble, flock together: concurrunt librarii: licet concurrant omnes philosophi, unite: trepidae comites, V.: summā cum expectatione concurritur: undique ex a…

concursatio.definition: concursātiō ōnis, f concurso, a running together, thronging: multa (populi): percontantium.—A collision, conflict: incidentium aliorum in alios, L.: utriusque exercitūs, Cs.: proelii, N. —A running about, going to and…

concursator.definition: concursātor ōris, m concurso, a skirmisher. hostis, L.: pedes, L.

concursio.definition: concursiō ōnis, f concurro, a concurrence, concourse: atomorum: crebra vocum. — Fig., in rhet., an emphatic repetition: in eadem verba.

concurso.definition: concursō —, —, āre, freq. concurro, to run to and fro, run about, fly around: urbe totā: dies noctīsque: per viam, L.: concursant praetores, travel about: in his administrandis rebus quam maxime concursari iubet, Cs.—…

concursus.definition: concursus ūs, m concurro, a running together, concourse, throng, mob, tumult: hominum: concursūs facere: magni domum ad Afranium fiebant, Cs.: in forum a totā urbe, L.: ingens, V.: undique, H.: in oppido.— An assault,…

concustoditus.definition: con-custōdītus P., closely watched, carefully guarded: a dracone, O.

concutio.definition: concutiō cussī, cussus, ere com- + quatio, to strike together: frameas, Ta.—To shake violently, shake, agitate, smite, shock: templa sonitu, T.: terra ingenti motu concussa, L.: oneratos messibus agros, O.: moenia, O.…

condecoro.definition: con-decorō —, —, āre, to grace, applaud, honor: ludos scenicos, T.

condemnatio.definition: condemnātiō ōnis, f condemno, a conviction, condemnation: Oppianici.

condemnator.definition: condemnātor ōris, m condemno, a prosecutor: Claudiae, Ta.

condemno.definition: condemnō āvī, ātus, are com- + damno, to convict, condemn, sentence, find guilty: omnes sine dubitatione condemnant: reum: alquem iudicio turpissimo: hunc sibi, for his own benefit: arbitrium pro socio condemnari, in …

condensus.definition: con-dēnsus adj., dense, close, thick, crowded: acies, L.: puppes litore, V.: columbae, V.: vallis arboribus, thickly covered, L.

condicio.definition: condiciō (not conditiō), ōnis, f com- + DIC-, an agreement, stipulation, condition, compact, proposition, terms, demand: pacis: non respuit condicionem, Cs.: ne si pax fieret, ipse per condiciones traderetur, S.: de c…

condico.definition: con-dīcō dīxī, dictus, ere, to agree, make an engagement, covenant, promise: patri patrato, L.: sic, Ta.: cum mihi condixisset, i. e. had promised to dine with me.

condimentum.definition: condīmentum ī, n condio, spice, seasoning: cibi.—Fig., spice, ornament, seasoning: amicitiae: sermonum facetiae: condimenti non nihil habere.

condio.definition: condiō īvī, ītus, īre condus (old), a butler, to make savory, season, spice, concoct: fungos: ius male condītum, H.: pulmentaria, Iu. — To make fragrant: unguenta. — To embalm: mortuos.— Fig., to cultivate, ornament, …

condiscipulatus.definition: condiscipulātus ūs, m condiscipulus, companionship in school, N.

condiscipulus.definition: con-discipulus ī, m a school - mate, fellowpupil: mens: generosi, N.

condisco.definition: con-discō didicī, —, ere, to learn well, learn thoroughly: modos, H.: crimen a teneris annis, O.: supplicare: pauperiem pati, H.: qui pecuniae fructus esset.

conditio2.definition: condītiō ōnis, f condio, a preserving: frugum.—A spicing, seasoning: ciborum.

conditor1.definition: conditor. ōris, m condo, a maker, builder, framer, establisher, founder, author, compiler: arcis, V.: cuius (oppidi), S.: urbis, L.: noster, L.: exit Conditor urbe suā, O.: Romani anni, i. e. author of the Fasti, O.: …

conditor2.definition: condītor ōris, m condio, a seasoner, pickler: negotii (a pun; cf. 1 conditor).

conditus1.definition: 'conditus adj. P. of condo, close, hidden, secret: praecordia, H.'

conditus2.definition: condītus adj. with comp. P. of condio, seasoned, savory: condī tiora facit haec: pyxis, chest of drugs, Iu. — Fig., of discourse, polished, ornamented: sermo: oratio lepore condītior: nemo suavitate condītior.

condo.definition: condō didī, ditus, ere com- + do, to put together, make by joining, found, establish, build, settle: oppida, H.: urbem: urbs condita vi et armis, L.: ante Romam conditam, before the foundation of Rome: post urbem cond…

condocefacio.definition: condocefaciō fēcī, factus, ere condoceo + facio, to train, teach, instruct, discipline: beluas: animum, ut, etc.

condolesco.definition: condolēscō luī, —, ēre, inch n. com- + doleo, to feel severe pain, suffer much, be in distress, ache: latus ei condoluisse: pes: caput, Tb.: temptatum frigore corpus, H.

condonatio.definition: condōnātiō ōnis, f condono, a giving away: bonorum possessionumque.

condono.definition: con-dōnō āvī, ātus, āre, to give, present, deliver, surrender, abandon: apothecas hominibus: hereditatem alicui, to adjudge. — To remit, acquit of: pecunias creditas debitoribus. — With two accs.: Argentum quod habes,…

condormio.definition: con-dormiō —, —, īre, to fall quite asleep, Cu.

conduco.definition: con-dūcō dūxī, ductus, ere, to draw together, assemble, collect, gather, unite: exercitum in unum locum, Cs.: viginti milia peditum, levy, L.: clientes eodem, Cs.: milites in unum, S.: vineas: cortice ramos, graft, O.…

conducticius.definition: conductīcius (not -tītius), adj. conduco, hired, mercenary: exercitus, N.: catervae, N.

conductio.definition: conductiō ōnis, f conduco, a bringing together, recapitulation, C. — A hiring, farming: (fundi): (vectigalium), L.

conductor.definition: conductor ōris, m conduco, a hirer, lessee, farmer, tenant.— Plur., Cs.—A contractor: operis.

conductum.definition: conductum ī, n conduco, something hired, the subject of a lease: alqd habere conducti, a hired apartment.

conductus.definition: (conductus ī),m P. of conduco. — Only plur, hirelings: operae conductorum: conducti plorant in funere, H. — Mercenary soldiers: conductorum III (milia), N.

conduplico.definition: con-duplicō āvī, —, āre, to double: quod boni promeritus fueris, T.: tenebrae conduplicantur: patrimonia, Iu.

conecto.definition: cōnectō (not connecto), —, nexus, ere com+ necto, to bind together, connect, entwine, join, unite, link: omnia inter se conexa: (apes) pedibus conexae ad limina pendent, V.: nodos, O.— Fig., to connect: amicitia cum v…

conexum.definition: cōnexum ī, m conecto, a necessary consequence, inevitable inference: ratio conexi.

conexus.definition: cōnexus (not conn-), adj. P. of conecto, adjoining: aedificia, Ta.

confabulor.definition: cōn-fābulor ātus, ārī, dep., to converse, have a talk (old).—Supin. acc.: ad eam accedere Confabulatum, T.

confarreo.definition: cōn-farreō —, ātus, āre, to marry by the ceremony of the cake (confarreatio, the offering of a cake of spelt, of which the parties partook): confarreandi adsuetudo, Ta.: confarreatis parentibus genite, Ta.

confatalis.definition: cōn-fātālis e, adj., associated by fate: res.

confectio.definition: cōnfectiō ōnis, f conficio, a finishing, preparing, composing, completing: huius libri: annalium: tributi, i. e. an exaction.—A consumption: escarum, a chewing.

confector.definition: cōnfector ōris, m conficio, an accomplisher, finisher: negotiorum, chargé d'affaires: belli.— A destroyer, consumer: omnium ignis.

confercio.definition: cōnferciō īre com- + farcio, see confertus.

confero.definition: cōn-ferō contulī, conlātus (coll-), cōnferre. I. To bring together, collect, gather, unite, join: ligna circa casam, N.: undique conlatis membris, H.: signis in unum locum conlatis, Cs.: dentes in corpore, join, O.: c…

confertim.definition: cōnfertim adv. confertus, in a compact body, closely: sese recipere, S.: pugnare, L.

confertus.definition: cōnfertus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of confercio, pressed close, crowded, thick, dense: cum ita conferta sint omnia, ut, etc.: plures simul, L.: agmen, V.—Close, compact, in close array: ut conferti proeliarentur, C…

confervesco.definition: cōnfervēscō ferbuī, —, ere, inch. com- + ferveo, to begin to boil, grow hot.—Fig.: mea cum conferbuit ira, H.

confessio.definition: cōnfessiō ōnis, f confiteor, a confession, acknowledgment: sua: servorum: confessionibus ipsius patefacta parricidia: ignorationis: captae pecuniae: culpae, L.: ea erat confessio caput rerum Romam esse, L.: tacita, L.

confessus.definition: cōnfessus adj. P. of confiteor, confessed: reus, who pleads guilty, O.: gladiatores.—Plur m. as subst, criminals who have confessed: de confessis supplicium sumere, S. — Confessed, acknowledged, certain: quam confessa…

confestim.definition: cōnfēstim adv. com- + FEN-, immediately, speedily, without delay, forthwith, suddenly: res gerenda: consequi: huc advolare: rex patres consulebat, L.: deletā materiā, L.: alacres admittier orant, V.: inclinatur acies, L.

conficiens.definition: cōnficiēns ntis, adj. with sup. P. of conficio, efficient, producing: causae: civitas conficientissima litterarum. — Plur n. as subst: (bonorum) conficientia, the sources.

conficio.definition: cōnficiō fēcī, fectus, ere com- + facio, to make ready, make, prepare, bring about, complete, accomplish, execute, consummate, fulfil: soccos suā manu: vestem: tabulae litteris Graecis confectae, written, Cs.: libri G…

confictio.definition: cōnfictiō ōnis, f confingo, a fabricating: criminis.

confidens.definition: cōnfīdēns entis, adj. with sup. P. of confido, bold, daring, confident: senex, T.—Shameless, audacious, impudent: Homo, T.: tumidusque, H.: astutia: iuvenum confidentissime, V.

confidenter.definition: cōnfīdenter adv. with comp. and sup. confidens, boldly, daringly, with intrepidity: dicere confidentius.—Audaciously, impudently, T.: confidentissime resistens, Her.

confidentia.definition: cōnfīdentia ae, f confidens, confidence, boldness: confidentiam et vocem defuisse.—Assurance, audacity, impudence: ingens, T.: quā confidentiā dicant.

confido.definition: cōn-fīdō fīsus, sum, ere, to trust, confide, rely upon, believe, be assured: vestrae virtuti: causae suae: cui (equitatui), Cs.: fidei Romanae, L.: Mario parum, S.: sibi confisi, relying on themselves, Cs.: si mihi ip…

configo.definition: cōn-fīgō fīxī, fīxus, ere, to join, fasten together: transtra trabibus confixa clavis, Cs.—To pierce through, transfix: capras sagittis: confixi ceciderunt, N.: Confixi a sociis, V.—Fig.: eius sententiis confixus, i. …

confindo.definition: cōn-findō —, —, ere, to cleave, split: pontus conscinditur aere, Tb.

confingo.definition: cōn-fingō finxī, fictus, ere, to fashion, fabricate, invent, devise, feign, pretend: lacrumae confictae dolis, T.: causas ad discordiam, T.: crimen: causam, L.: id cogitatum esse.

confinis.definition: cōn-fīnis e, adj., bordering, conterminous, adjoining, contiguous: ager, L.: hi Senonibus, Cs.: potentiori, S.: caput collo, O.: litora prato, O.— Fig., nearly related, like, similar: carmina studio vestro, O.

confinium.definition: cōnfīnium ī, n confinis, a confine, common boundary, limit, border: Treverorum, Cs.: Germaniae Raetiaeque, Ta.: in vicinitatibus et confiniis aequus, in questions of: triplicis confinia mundi, O.—Fig., a confine, boun…

confio.definition: cōn-fīō —, fierī, collat. form for conficior, to be brought together: ex quo summa mercedis confieret, might be raised, L. — To be arranged, be accomplished, be brought about: id difficilius, Cs.: quā ratione quod ins…

confirmatio.definition: cōnfīrmātiō ōnis, f confirmo, a securing, establishing, confirming: auctoritatis: libertatis. — In rhet., an adducing of proofs, C. — A confirmation, assurance, encouragement: animi, Cs.: mea: perfugae, by a refugee, Cs.

confirmator.definition: cōnfīrmātor ōris, m confirmo, he who assures: pecuniae, a surety.

confirmatus.definition: cōnfīrmātus adj. with comp. P. of confirmo, encouraged, confident, courageous, resolute: animus: confirmatiorem exercitum efficere, Cs.— Established, certain: quod eo confirmatius erit, si, etc.

confirmo.definition: cōn-fīrmō āvī, ātus, āre, to make firm, make strong, establish, strengthen: vires nervosque, Cs.: confirmandi causā , Cs.—Fig., to strengthen, establish, reinforce, confirm: se, to recover: valetudinem: cum civitatibu…

confisio.definition: cōnfīsiō ōnis, f confido, confidence, assurance: animi.

confiteor.definition: cōnfiteor fessus, ērī, dep. com- + fateor, to acknowledge, confess, own, avow, concede, allow, grant: confitere, T.: confitentem audire alqm: non infitiando confiteri videbantur: Confessas manūs tendens, in surrender,…

conflagro.definition: cōn-flagrō āvī, ātus, āre, to burn, be consumed, be on fire: impedimenta conflagrare, Cs.: classis incendio conflagrabat: urbem conflagrare velle: urbs incendio conflagrata, Her. — Fig., to be inflamed, burn: amoris f…

conflictio.definition: cōnflīctiō ōnis, f confligo, a collision, conflict: causarum: rerum contrariarum.

conflicto.definition: cōnflīctō āvī, ātus, āre, intens. confligo, to come in conflict, collide: cum nialo, T.: per scelera rem p., to ruin, Ta.

conflictor.definition: cōnflīctor ātus, ārī, dep. confligo, to struggle, wrestle, conflict, engage, be afflicted: cum ingeniis eiusmodi, T.: cum adversā fortunā, N.: inopiā, Cs.: morbo, N.: difficultatibus, L.: tempestatibus, Ta.—To contend…

conflictus2.definition: (cōnflīctus ūs), m confligo, a striking together (only abl sing.): lapidum.—A wrestling, struggle: corporum.

confligo.definition: cōn-flīgō flīxī, flīctus, ere, to come into collision, dash together: illae (naves) inter se incitatae conflixerunt, Cs.— To be in conflict, contend, fight, combat: armis: angusto mari, N.: manu cum hoste: cum Antonio…

conflo.definition: cōn-flō āvī, ātus, āre, to blow up, kindle, light: incendium, L.: falces conflantur in ensem, are smelted, V. — Fig., to kindle, inflame: mihi invidiam: civile bellum conflatum tuā operā : seditionem.—To bring togethe…

confluens.definition: cōnfluēns entis, m P. of confluo, a place of union, confluence, junction, forks: ad confluentem Mosae et Rheni, Cs.: ad confluentes conlocat, etc., L.

confluo.definition: cōn-fluō fluxī, —, ere, to flow together, run together: ibi amnes confluunt in unum, L.: (portūs) in exitu confluunt.—Fig., to flock together, crowd, throng, assemble, be gathered: ad eum, Cs.: ad eius triremem, N.: R…

confodio.definition: cōn-fodiō fōdī, fossus, ere. — Prop., to dig up, dig over; hence, to transfix, stab, pierce: ibique pugnans confoditur, S.: aliquot volneribus, L.: confossus, V.: alqm harpe, O.—Fig., to transfix: tot iudiciis confoss…

confore.definition: cōnfore inf. com- + fore, inf fut. of sum, only impers, that it will be accomplished: et spero confore, i. e. to succeed, T.

conformatio.definition: cōnfōrmātiō ōnis, f conformo, a symmetrical forming, conformation, shape, form, fashion: liniamentorum: vocis, expression: doctrinae, i. e. culture.—Fig., an idea, notion, conception: animi: ut res conformatio quaedam…

conformo.definition: cōn-fōrmō āvī, ātus, āre, to form, fashion, shape: mundus a naturā conformatus. — Fig., to fashion, educate, modify, form: mentem cogitatione: mores: vocem hortatu: liberos sibi, Ta.: se ad alcuius voluntatem, to conf…

confragosus.definition: cōn - fragōsus adj., broken, rough, uneven: loca, L.: viae, L.—Plur n. as subst: inter confragosa (sc. loca), L.

confremo.definition: cōn-fremō uī, —, ere, to resound, murmur loudly: confremuere omnes, O.

confrico.definition: cōn-fricō āvī, ātus, āre, to rub vigorously: caput unguento.

confringo.definition: cōnfringō frēgī, frāctus, ere com-+frango, to break in pieces, shatter: forīs caedendo, L.: digitos.—Fig., to destroy, crush: consilia.

confugio.definition: cōn-fugiō fūgī, —, ere, to flee, take refuge, run for succor: domum, T.: ad te, V.: ad aram in exsilium: Phylen, N.: in naves, Cs.: ad limina supplex, O. — Fig., to take refuge, have recourse, resort: ad vim: ad Etrus…

confugium.definition: cōnfugium ī, n com-+2 FVG-, a place of refuge, refuge, shelter, O.

confundo.definition: cōn-fundō fūdī, fūsus, ere, to pour together, mingle, mix, blend: ius confusum sectis herbis, H.: (venenum) in poculo confusum: Cumque tuis lacrimis nostras, O.: (Alpheus) Siculis confunditur undis, mingles, V.—To pou…

confuse.definition: cōnfūsē adv. with comp. confusus, confusedly, in disorder: loqui: agere: confusius acta res.

confusio.definition: cōnfūsiō ōnis, f confusus, a mingling, mixing, blending: virtutum. — A confounding, confusion, disorder: temporum: suffragiorum: vitae: oris, i. e. a blush, Ta.

confusus.definition: cōnfūsus adj. with comp. P. of confundo, mingled, confused, perplexed, disorderly: strages, V.: oratio: verba, O.: suffragium, L.: clamor, of doubtful origin, L. — Disordered, confused: mens, V.: animo, L.: variā imag…

confuto.definition: cōnfūtō āvī, ātus, āre com- + FV-, to check, repress, dampen, suppress, diminish: dolores memoriā: audaciam.— To put down, put to silence, confute, refute, overthrow: verbis senem, T.: dictis confutabitur, T.: argumen…

confutuo.definition: cōn-futuō —, —, ere, to cohabit with, Ct.

congelo.definition: con-gēlō āvī, ātus, āre, to freeze together, congeal: cum duro lingua palato Congelat, stiffens, O.: alqd congelat aëre tacto, is petrified, O.—Fig., to grow stiff: congelasse amicum otio.— To freeze, make stiff: in l…

congemino.definition: con-geminō āvī, ātus, āre, to redouble, multiply: ensibus ictūs, V.: securim, ply, V.

congemo.definition: con-gemō uī, —, ere, to sigh deeply: congemuit senatus: (ornus) supremum Congemuit, V.

conger.definition: conger grī, m, =go/ggros, a sea-eel, conger-eel, T.

congeries.definition: congeriēs acc. em, abl. ē, f com- + GES-, a heap, pile, mass: disposita, i. e. chaos, O.: Congerie e mediā, the ruins, O.: lapidum, L.: summa silvae, O.

congero.definition: con-gerō gessī, gestus, ere, to bring together, collect, heap up, throw together: vim auri in regnum: undique quod, etc., N.: congestis undique saccis, H.: turea dona, V.: viaticum: congestis armis, O.: in suam sua vi…

congesticius.definition: congestīcius adj. congero, heaped, piled up, thrown together: agger ex materiā.

congestus2.definition: (congestus ūs), m com-+GES-, a bringing together, heaping, accumulation (only abl sing.) copiarum, Ta.: avium: lapidum, Ta.

congiarium.definition: congiārium ī, n congius, a largess to the poor of a congius to each man (of oil, etc.): congiariis multitudinem delenire.—A largess in money, gift, distribution: ab Antonio: plebi, Ta.: molitum, Cu.: multa, L.

congius.definition: congius ī, m a measure for liquids, six sextarii (nearly six pints English): olei, L.

conglacio.definition: con-glaciō —, —, āre, to freeze, congeal: aqua conglaciaret frigoribus.

conglobatio.definition: conglobātiō ōnis, f conglobo, a crowding together: fortuita (militum), Ta.

conglobo.definition: con-globō āvī, ātus, āre, to gather into a ball, press together in a mass, roll up: mare conglobatur undique: terra nutibus suis conglobata: se in unum, L.: in forum, L.: proditores conglobati, in a compact body, L.: …

conglutinatio.definition: conglūtinātiō ōnis, f conglutino, a cementing, joining: verborum. — A union, compound: recens.

conglutino.definition: con-glūtinō āvī, ātus, āre, to join together, unite, cement: amores nuptiis, T. — To compose, unite, frame together: hominem: amicitias: Ex his conglutinatus, composed.

congratulor.definition: con-grātulor ātus, ārī, dep., to wish joy, congratulate: libertatem civitati restitutam, L.

congredior.definition: congredior gressus, ī, dep. com- + gradior, to come together, meet, have an interview: Congredere actutum, T.: ubi congressi sunt: coram: cum eo ad conloquium, L.: in itinere, Cs. — To meet in strife, fight, contend, …

congregabilis.definition: congregābilis e, adj. congrego, social, gre garious: apium examina.

congregatio.definition: congregātiō ōnis, f congrego, union, society, association: hominum.

congrego.definition: congregō āvī, atus, are com- + grex, to collect in a flock, swarm: apium examina congregantur.—To collect, assemble, unite, join, associate: homines: familiae congregantur: se unum in locum ad curiam: hominem in hunc …

congressio.definition: congressiō ōnis, f com- + GRAD-, a meeting, interview, conference, association, society: nostra: congressione dignus: eum congressions prohibere: in congressionibus familiarum, in familiar circles: maris et feminae.

congressus2.definition: congressus ūs, m com- + GRAD-, a meeting, assembly, conference, conversation, interview: congressum tuum fugiunt: ad congressum eius pervenire: cum illis sermone et congressu coniungi: congressu aequalium prohibitus, …

congruens.definition: congruēns entis, adj. P. of congruo, agreeing, fit, appropriate, suitable, consistent, congruous: cum iis naturā: actio menti: genus dicendi: motus, appropriate gesture, L.: haec duo pro congruentibus sumere: congruen…

congruenter.definition: 'congruenter adv. congruens, agreeably, fitly, suitably: naturae vivere: ad alqd dicere.'

congruo.definition: congruō uī, —, ere, to coincide, agree: dies cum solis ratione: ut ad metam eandem solis dies congruerent, L.—Fig., to coincide, correspond, be suited, be adapted, agree, accord, suit, fit: alcuius cum moribus, to be …

conicio.definition: cōniciō or cōiciō (coniiciō), iēcī, iectus, ere com-+iacio. I. To throw together, unite, collect: sarcinas in medium, L. — Fig., to draw a conclusion, conclude, infer, conjecture, guess: sexaginta ut conicio, T.: eum …

coniectio.definition: coniectiō ōnis, f com- + IA-, a hurling, throwing: telorum. — Fig., a putting together, comparing: annonae et aestimationis.—A conjecture, interpretation: somniorum.

coniecto.definition: coniectō āvī, ātus, āre, freq. conicio, to infer, conjecture, guess: alqd: rem eventu, L.: de imperio, Ta.: eum Aegyptum iter habere, Cs.: ex eo quid sentiant, L.: valetudinem ex eo, quod, etc., Ta.

coniector.definition: coniector ōris, m conicio, a diviner, seer, soothsayer.

coniectura.definition: coniectūra ae, f conicio, a conjecture, guess, induction, inference: ex uno de ceteris: coniecturam facere: ex voltu coniecturam facere, quantum, etc.: num aberret a coniecturā suspitio, i. e. reasonable inference: co…

coniecturalis.definition: coniectūrālis e, adj. coniectura, belonging to conjecture, conjectural: causa.

coniectus2.definition: coniectus ūs, m com- + IA-, a throwing, casting, projecting, hurling: lapidum coniectu fracta domus: terrae, L.: telorum, N.: venire ad teli coniectum, within reach, L.—Fig., a turning, directing: in me animorum oculo…

conifer.definition: cōnifer fera, ferum, adj. conus + FER-, bearing conical fruit: cyparissi, V.

coniger.definition: cōniger gera, gerum, adj. conus + gero, bearing conical fruit: pinus, Ct.

conitor.definition: cōnītor (not conn-), nīsus or nīxus, ī com- + nitor, dep., to put forth all one's strength, make an effort, strive, struggle, endeavor: omnes conisi hostem avertunt, L.: valido corpore: dextrā, V.: omnibus copiis, L.:…

coniugalis.definition: coniugālis e, adj. coniunx, of marriage, conjugal: di, Ta.: amor, Ta.

coniugatio.definition: coniugātiō ōnis, f coniugo.—Prop., a connection; hence, the etymological connection of words.

coniugator.definition: coniugātor ōris, m com- + IV-, one who unites: amoris, Ct.

coniugialis.definition: coniugiālis e, adj. coniugium, of marriage, connubial: foedus, O.: festa, O.

coniugium.definition: coniugium ī n com- + IV-.—Prop., a connection, union; hence, marriage, wedlock: Tulliae: liberale, T.: coniugii dos, O.—Of animals, V.— A husband, V., Pr.—A wife, V.

coniugo.definition: con-iugō āvī, ātus, āre, to join, unite: amicitiam, to form: coniugata verba, etymologically related.

coniuncte.definition: coniūnctē adv. with comp. and sup. coniungo, in connection, conjointly, at the same time: coniuncte re verboque risus moveatur: elatum aliquid, i. e. conditionally: agere.—In friendship, intimately: coniuncte vivere, …

coniunctim.definition: coniūnctim adv. coniungo, unitedly, in common, jointly, together: pecuniae coniunctim ratio habetur, Cs.: petere auxilium, N.: rogationes accipere, L.

coniunctio.definition: coniūnctiō ōnis, f com- + IV-, a connecting, uniting, union, agreement: hominum: adfinitatis: vestra equitumque: mecum gratiae.— Marriage, relationship, affinity: sanguinis: fratrum: adfinitatis.—Friendship, intimacy:…

coniunctum.definition: coniūnctum ī, n coniungo. — In rhet., connection.

coniunctus.definition: coniūnctus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of coniungo, connected: ratis coniuncta crepidine saxi Expositis scalis, V.—Of places, adjoining, bordering upon, near, close: loca castris, Cs.: Paphlagonia Cappadociae, N. — Co…

coniungo.definition: con-iungō iūnxī, iūnctus, ere, to fasten together, connect, join, unite, gather: calamos cerā, V.: eam epistulam cum hac: huic (navi) alteram, Cs.: dextrae dextram, O.—Fig., to join, unite, associate: cohortes cum exe…

coniunx.definition: coniūnx or coniux iugis, m and f com- + IV-, a married person, consort, spouse, husband, wife: coniuges et liberi: mulier cum suo coniuge: quo coniuge felix ferar, O.: mea: avara.—Of animals, the female, O.—A betrothe…

coniuratio.definition: coniūrātiō ōnis, f coniuro, a uniting in an oath, sworn union, alliance: nobilitatis, Cs.: de bello, L.: (mulierum), common understanding, T. —A conspiracy, plot, secret combination: Catilinae, S.: impia, L.: coniurat…

coniuratus.definition: coniūrātus adj. P. of coniuro, bound together by an oath, associate, allied, conspiring: homines: Agmina, O.: rates, of allies, O.: in proditionem, L.—Poet., with inf: Graecia coniurata rumpere nuptias, H.: caelum res…

coniuro.definition: con-iūrō āvī, ātus, āre, to swear together, swear in a body (of a levy en masse): ut iuniores Italiae coniurarent, Cs.— To swear together, combine under oath: omne Coniurat Latium, V.: inter se nihil acturos, etc., Cs…

coniveo.definition: cōnīveō (not conn-), —, ēre, to shut the eyes, blink: somno: altero oculo.—Of the eyes, to close, shut, be heavy: coniventes oculi: (oculis) somno coniventibus.—Fig., to be dull, drowse, be languid: blandimenta, quibu…

conlabefacto.definition: con-labefactō (coll-) —, —, āre, to convulse, break down: vastum onus (montis), O.

conlabefio.definition: con-labefīō (coll-) factus, fierī, pass, to fall to pieces, collapse, be ruined: ut (navis) conlabefieret, Cs.—Fig.: a Themistocle conlabefactus, overthrown, N.

conlabor.definition: con-lābor (coll-) lapsus, ī, to fall together, fall in ruins, crumble: moenia conlapsa ruinā sunt, L.: urbes motu terrae, Ta.: postquam conlapsi cineres, V. — Fig., to fall, sink: conlapsa membra referre, V.: subito d…

conlaceratus.definition: 'con-laceratus (coll-) adj., torn to pieces: corpus, Ta.'

conlacrimatio.definition: conlacrimātiō (coll-) ōnis, f conlacrimo, a sympathetic weeping.

conlacrimo.definition: conlacrimō (coll-, -lacrumō) āvī, —, ā re, to weep in sympathy, lament together, T., C.—To bewail: casum meum: casum suum, L.

conlactea.definition: con - lactea (coll-, -tia) ae, f com- + lacteus, a foster-sister, Iu.

conlatio.definition: conlātiō (coll-) ōnis, f conlatus, a bringing together, hostile meeting, collision: signorum.— A contribution, collection: decimae, L.: exempti conlationibus, Ta.—Fig., a comparison, similitude. —In philos.: rationis,…

conlaudatio.definition: conlaudātiō (coll-) ōnis, f conlaudo, warm praise, eulogy. hominis.

conlaudo.definition: con - laudō (coll-) āvī, ātus, āre, to prize highly, extol: filium, T.: factum suis: militum virtutem, L.: alqm magnifice, L.: me, H.: conlaudatis militibus, Cs.: conlaudandus, quod, etc.

conlecta.definition: conlēcta (coll-) ae, f conlectus, a contribution, collection: a convivā exigere.

conlecticius.definition: conlēctīcius (coll-; not -titius) um, adj. conlectus, gathered in haste, huddled together: exercitus.

conlectio.definition: conlēctiō (coll-) ōnis, f conlectus, a collecting, gathering: (membrorum).—Fig., in rhet., a summing up, recapitulation.

conlega.definition: conlēga or collēga ae, m com- + 3 LEG-, a partner in office, colleague, associate, assessor: in censurā: imperii, Ta.: conlegam habere: post me sedet, H.: dux delectus est, duo collegae dati, N. —An associate, compani…

conlegium.definition: conlēgium or collēgium ī, n conlega, association in office, colleagueship: expertus mihi concordi collegio vir, L.: consul per tot collegia expertus, L.—An official body, association, board, bench, college, guild, cor…

contrectatio.definition: contrectātiō (contract-) ōnis, f contrecto, a touching, contact: equae.

contrecto.definition: contrectō (contractō) āvī, ātus, āre com+tracto, to touch, handle, come in contact with, feel: pectora, O.: (liber) contrectatus manibus volgi, H.: contrectata pudicitia, violated, Ta.: corpus oculis volgi contrectand…

contremisco.definition: con-tremīscō muī, —, ere, inch, to tremble, shake, shudder: totā mente: metu, S.: omne Contremuit nemus, V.—Fig.: cuius numquam fides contremuit, wavered: periculum, shudder at, H.

contremo.definition: con-tremō —, —, ere, to tremble, quake: caelum tonitru contremit, Pac. ap. C.

contribuo.definition: con-tribuō tribuī, tribūtus, ere, to unite, incorporate, associate, enroll together: cum Oscensibus contributi, Cs.: Phocenses iis contribuerunt, L.: Corinthum in anticum gentis concilium, L.: urbes ad condendam Megal…

contristo.definition: contrīstō āvī, ātus, āre com-+tristis, to sadden, make gloomy, cloud, dim, darken: frigore caelum, V.: (Aquarius) annum, H.

contritus.definition: contrītus adj. P. of contero, worn out, trite, common: praecepta: proverbium vetustate. — Worthless: praemium.

controversia.definition: contrōversia (-vorsia) ae, f controversus, a contention, quarrel, question, dispute, controversy, debate: privata: rem in controversiam vocare: re in controversiam deductā, Cs.: in controversiam venire: dirimere contr…

controversiosus.definition: contrōversiōsus adj. controversia, much controverted: res, L.

controversus.definition: contrōversus adj. contro- (cf. contra)+versus, disputed, questionable, undecided: ius: res: auspicium, L.—Disputatious: gens naturā (dub.).

contrucido.definition: con-trucīdō āvī, ātus, are, to cut to pieces, cut down, put to the sword: corpore contrucidato.— Fig.: rem p.

contrudo.definition: con-trūdō sī, sus, ere, to thrust, crowd together: aliquos in balneas.

contubernalis.definition: contubernālis is, m and f com-+taberna, a tent-companion, messmate (usu. ten men and a decanus in one tent), C., Ta., Cu.—A personal follower, attendant: Pompeio.—A comrade, companion, associate, colleague: tui: meus …

contubernium.definition: contubernium ī, n com-+taberna, companionship in a tent, the relation of a general and his personal follower: contuberni necessitudo: patris, S.: alqm contubernio aestimare, by intimate companionship, Ta.: militum, wi…

contueor.definition: con-tueor uitus, ērī, dep., to look on, gaze upon, behold, survey: contuemini os, look him in the face: alqm oculis: id novum contuens, observing this novelty, N.—Fig., to contemplate, regard: a contuendis malis avoca…

contuitus.definition: (contuitus ūs), m a beholding.—Only abl sing.: parricidarum, Cu.

contumacia.definition: contumācia ae, f contumax, inflexibility, contumacy, obstinacy, stubbornness: illa tua: in voltu, L.: responsi: adversus principem, Ta.— Firmness, constancy: libera.

contumaciter.definition: contumāciter adv. with comp. contumax, obstinately, stubbornly: scribere: omnia agere, L.: contumacius se gerere, N.

contumax.definition: contumāx ācis, adj. with comp. com-+ 1 TEM-, insolent, unyielding, obstinate, stiff-necked: quis contumacior?: animus, Ta.: voltus, Cu.: lima, Ph.

contumelia.definition: contumēlia ae, f com-+1 TEM-, insult, abuse, affront, reproach, invective, contumely: ei facere contumeliam, T.: contumelias dicere, L.: improborum: tam insignem in me accipere, T.: tantā adfectus: tantā acceptā , Cs.…

contumeliose.definition: contumēliōsē adv. with comp. and sup. contumeliosus, abusively, insolently: hoc dicere: contumeliosius facta iniuria, T.: contumeliosissime ei male dicere.

contumeliosus.definition: contumēlīōsus adj. with comp. contumelia, full of abuse, reproachful, abusive, insulting: contumeliosis vocibus prosequi, Cs.: in edictis: te esse dicunt contumeliosum, quod, etc.: oratio: quod contumeliosum in eos fo…

contumulo.definition: con - tumulō —, —, āre, to cover with a mound, inter, bury: contumulari humo, O.

contundo.definition: con-tundō tudī, tūsus or tūnsus, ere, to beat, bruise, grind, crush, pound, break to pieces: pugiles caestibus contusi: Vos saxis, H.: pectus ictu, O.: flos nullo contusus aratro, Ct.: contusi inter saxa, L.: narī s a…

conturbatio.definition: conturbātiō ōnis, f conturbo, confusion, disquiet, consternation: mentis: est metus excutiens cogitata.

conturbatus.definition: conturbātus adj. with comp. P. of conturbo, distracted, disordered, confused, disquieted: oculus: homo: discedit, in confusion: in scribendo conturbatior.

conturbo.definition: con-turbō āvī, ātus, āre, to confuse, disturb, derange, disorder, confound: ordines (militum), S.: rem p., S.—Fig., to disturb, disquiet: mihi Rationes, upset my plans, T.: te.—Esp., in business, with ellips. of ratio…

contus.definition: contus ī, m, konto/s, a pole, pike: conti bini a prorā prominentes, L.—As a weapon, V.: contis praefixa capita, Ta.—A boat-hook, V.

conubialis.definition: cōnūbiālis (not connū-), e, adj. conubium, of wedlock, conjugal: iura, O.

conubium.definition: cōnūbium (not connū-), n com-+nubo, marriage, wedlock (as a civil institution; cf. coniugium, the personal union), C.: per conubia Gaetulos secum miscuere, S.: natae, V.: nostra, with me, O.: Pyrrhin' conubia servas? …

conus.definition: cōnus ī, m, kw=nos, a cone: coni forma.— The apex of a helmet, V.

convalesco.definition: con-valēscō luī, ere, inch, to recover, regain health, grow strong, gain strength: ilico: ex morbo: de volnere, O.: hoc spatio, Cs.: in dies: ignis convaluit, O.: ut convalescere civitas posset: mens, O.: opinio de al…

convallis.definition: 'con - vallis is, f a valley, ravine, dell, C.: magna, Cs.: interiectae collibus convalles, L.: depressae, V.'

convaso.definition: con-vāsō āvī, —, āre com-+vasa, to pack together, pack up: aliquid, T.

convecto.definition: convectō —, —, āre, freq. conveho, to carry together, heap together: recentīs praedas, V.: ligones ex agris, Ta.

conveho.definition: con-vehō vexī, vectus, ere, to carry together, collect, store: frumentum ex regionibus in urbem, Cs.: frumentum Capuam, L.: lintribus in eam insulam materiem: ex ante convecto sufficere, previous stores, L.—Pass, to b…

convello.definition: con-vellō vellī, volsus or vulsus, to tear away, pluck up, pull off, wrest, rend: vectibus saxa turris, Cs.: gradūs Castoris: aesculum, V.: glaebam vomere, Ct.: repagula: signa, to pluck up (in decamping), L.: simulac…

convenae.definition: convenae ārum, m and f com-+BA-, VEN-, assembled strangers, refugees, vagabonds: convenas congregasse: convenarum plebs, L.

conveniens.definition: conveniēns entis, adj. P. of convenio, agreeing, consistent, corresponding: hunc superbum habitum convenientes sequebantur contemptūs aures, etc., L.: recta et convenientia natura desiderat: sibi convenientia finge, H…

convenienter.definition: convenienter adv. conveniens, fitly, suitably, conformably, consistently: dici: cum eā (naturā) vivere: naturae, H.: ad fortunae statum loqui, L.

convenientia.definition: convenientia ae, f conveniens, agreement, harmony, symmetry: naturae: rerum in amicitiā: naturae cum extis.

convenio.definition: con-veniō vēnī, ventus, īre, to come together, meet, assemble, gather, come in a body: ex provinciā, Cs.: ad Caesarem gratulatum, Cs.: ad eum defendendum, N.: Romam Italia tota convenit: unum in locum, Cs.: in consili…

conventicius.definition: conventīcius adj. 1 conventus, of assembling, for attendance; hence, as subst n. (sc. aes), money paid for attending an assembly.

conventiculum.definition: conventiculum ī, n dim. 2 conventus, a petty assembly, association: hominum.—A place of assembling: conventicula exstruere, Ta.

conventio.definition: conventiō ōnis, f com-+BA-, VEN-, an agreement, compact, convention, L., Ta.

conventum.definition: conventum ī, n 1 conventus, an agreement, compact, contract, convention: stare conventis: testes-conventorum, L.: pacti et conventi formula: Conventum et pactum, a marriage contract and settlement, Iu.

conventus2.definition: conventus ūs, m com-+BA-, VEN-, a meeting, assembly, throng: comitum, T.: virorum mulierumque: primo conventu, S.: conventu pro solitudine abuti: natum Conventūs trahit in medios, V.: ridetur ab omni Conventu, H.—A co…

converbero.definition: con-verberō āvī, ātus, āre, to strike, beat: os suum, Cu.

converro.definition: con-verrō (-vorrō) ī, —, ere, to sweep together: alqd sabuli, Cu.—To gather in, gain: hereditates.

conversatio.definition: conversātiō ōnis, f converso, familiar intercourse, association (late): mortalium, Ta.

conversio.definition: conversiō ōnis, f com-+VERT-, a turning round, revolving, revolution: caeli: mensium. — Fig., a subversion, alteration, change: rerum: tempestatum: rei p.—In rhet.: in extremum, repetition at the end of a clause: orat…

converso.definition: conversō —, —, āre, freq. conversus, to turn around: animus se ipse conversans.

conversor.definition: con - versor ātus, ārī, to abide, frequent: in regiā , Cu.

converto.definition: con-vertō (-vortō) tī, sus, ere.—Trans, to turn round, cause to turn, turn back, reverse, direct: in infimo orbe luna convertitur: vox Herculem convertit, L.: ter se, O.: vias, V.: caeli conversa per auras, wheeled, V…

convestio.definition: con-vestiō īvī, ītus, īre, to clothe, cover, envelop: herbis prata convestirier: domus lucis convestita, surrounded: omnia hederā.

convexus.definition: convexus adj. conveho, vaulted, arched, rounded, convex, concave: caelum, O.: trames silvae, V.: foramina terrae, O.—As subst n., a vault, arch, hollow: in convexo nemorum, V.: caeli convexa, the vaulted arch, V.: ut …

conviciator.definition: convīciātor (convīt-) ōris, m convicior, a railer, reviler.

convicior.definition: convīcior (convīt-) ātus, ārī, dep. convicium, to revile, reproach, taunt, rail at, L.

convicium.definition: convīcium (not-vītium), ī, n com-+VOC-, a loud noise, cry, clamor, outcry: cum maximo convitio: alcui fit a senatu: cantorum: Humanae convicia linguae, utterances, O.—Of frogs, Ph.— Wrangling, altercation, contention:…

convictio.definition: convīctiō ōnis, f com-+VIV-, companionship, intercourse, intimacy, C.—A companion: convictiones domesticae.

convictor.definition: convīctor ōris, m com-+VIV-, a table companion, messmate, familiar friend, H., C.

convictus2.definition: convīctus ūs, m com-+VIV-, a living together, intimacy, social intercourse: humanus: longi convictibus aevi, O.—A banquet, feast: convictibus indulgere, Ta.: sobrii, Ta.: omnis Convictus ... De Rutilo, the talk of eve…

convinco.definition: con-vincō vīcī, vīctus, ere, to overcome, convict, refute, expose: me teste: paulatim convictus veris, L.: convicti mulctantur, when convicted, Ta.: te amentiae: convicti maleficii servi: facinoris, S.: manifestis cri…

conviso.definition: con-vīsō —, —, ere, to shine upon, C. poet.

conviva.definition: convīva ae, m and f com-+VIV-, a table companion, guest: ridere convivae: satur, H.: frequens, O.: ebrius, O.: promissus, promised guest, Iu.

convivalis.definition: convīvālis e, adj. conviva, of a guest, festal, convivial: oblectamenta, L.: fabulae, Ta.

convivator.definition: convīvātor ōris, m convivor, a host, entertainer, master of a feast, H., L.

convivium.definition: convīvium ī, n com-+VIV-, a meal in company, social feast, entertainment, banquet: egit vitam in conviviis, T.: muliebria: ornare: in convivio saltare: Mutua convivia, V.: capilli propter convivia pexi, for company, I…

convivor.definition: convīvor ātus, ārī, dep. conviva, to banquet, revel, carouse together: crebro, T.: in publico, de publico.

convocatio.definition: convocātiō ōnis, f convoco, a convoking, calling together, assembling: populi R.

convoco.definition: con-vocō āvī, ātus, āre, to call together, convoke, assemble, summon: milites: senatum in aedem: principes Trevirorum ad se, Cs.: principes penes Laecam, S.: convocato consilio, Cs.: ad contionem, L.

convolnero.definition: con-volnerō āvī, ātum, āre, to wound severely: iumenta, Cu.

convolo.definition: con-volō āvī, ātus, āre, to fly together, come hastily together, run together: populus convolat, T.: ad rostra: ad sellas consulum, L.

convolvo.definition: con-volvō volvī, volūtus, ere, to roll together, roll up, roll round: se (sol): Lubrica terga (coluber), V.: pennis convolvitur Ales.— To fasten together, interweave, interlace: testudo convoluta omnibus rebus, quibus…

convomo.definition: con-vomō —, —, ere, to bespew, vomit upon: mensas: maritum, Iu.

cooperio.definition: cooperiō ruī, rtus, īre com-+operio, to cover, cover over, overwhelm, bury: Cyrsilum lapidibus: ab exercitu lapidibus cooperiri, L.: atrā nube coopertum, Ta.—P. pass., buried, involved, covered: sceleribus: miseriis, …

cooptatio.definition: cooptātiō ōnis, f coopto, an election to office, appointment, choice: collegiorum: censoria, by the censors: in Patres, L.

coopto.definition: cooptō āvī, ātus, āre com-+opto, to choose, elect, admit by election, appoint to office: senatores: novum senatum: tribunos plebis, L.: alqm tribunum, L.: magistrum equitum, L.: in conlegium (augurum): in locum augura…

coorior.definition: coorior ortus, īrī, dep. com-+orior, to come forth, stand up, arise, appear, rise, break forth: ignes pluribus simul locis, L.: bellum in Galliā , Cs.: certamen, O.: seditio coorta, L.—To arise, break out, begin: tant…

cophinus.definition: cophinus ī m, ko/finos, a basket, Iu.

copia.definition: cōpia ae, f com-+ops, an abundance, ample supply, plenty: frumenti, Cs.: navium magna, Cs.: bona librorum, H.: nullā ferramentorum copiā, in the scarcity of, Cs.—Resources, wealth, supplies, riches, prosperity: domest…

copiose.definition: cōpiōsē adv. with comp. and sup. copiosus, in great abundance, copiously, abundantly, plentifully: comparare pastum: profectus erat, richly provided: ornatus, by a large majority: Capitolium copiosius ornatum.—Of disc…

copiosus.definition: cōpiōsus adj. with comp. and sup. copia, furnished abundantly, well supplied, having abundance, rich, copious, plentiful, abounding: familiae: via copiosa omniumque rerum abundans, N.: stativa, L.: patrimonium: victus…

copis.definition: copis idis, f, kopi/s, a short, curved sword, yataghan, Cu.

copo1.definition: cōpō ōnis, m CAP-, a petty tradesman, huckster, innkeeper: ad cauponem devertere: Perfidus, H.: copo de viā Latinā.

copula.definition: cōpula ae, f com-+AP-, a band, rope, thong, tie, fastening: copulā vinctus, N.: Copula detrahitur canibus, O.: copulis continebantur (naves), grapnel-hooks, Cs.—A bond, tie: inrupta tenet (of love), H.: talium virorum…

copulatio.definition: cōpulātiō ōnis, f copulo, a coupling, connecting: atomorum inter se.—Fig., association.

copulatus.definition: cōpulātus adj. with comp. P. of copulo, joined, united, connected: quaedam (opp. simplicia): verba: nihil copulatius quam, etc.

copulo.definition: cōpulō āvī, ātus, āre copula, to couple, bind, tie together, join, connect, unite: hominem cum beluā: altera ratis huic copulata est, L.: copulati in ius pervenimus, face to face. — Fig., to join, connect, unite: verb…

coquo.definition: coquō coxī, coctus, ere COC-, to cook, prepare by cooking, bake, boil, roast, parch, steep, melt, heat: cena ei coquebatur, N.: cibaria, L.: coctus cibus, S.: venena, L.: aere cavo, O.: liba in foro, O.—To burn, parch…

coquus.definition: coquus (coquos, cocus) ī, m COC-, a cook: coqui, T., C., L.

cor.definition: cor cordis (no gen plur.), n CARD-, the heart: sine corde esse: gemitū s alto de corde petiti, O.—Plur, persons, souls (poet.): fortissima, V.: aspera, V.—Fig., the heart, soul, mind: meo Cordi carior, T.: stupor cord…

coram.definition: cōram adv. and praep. com-+ōs. I. Adv., in the presence, before the eyes, in the face, openly, face to face: coram in os te laudare, T.: coram me praesente dicere: se ipse coram offert, i. e. before the soldiers, L.: …

corbis.definition: corbis is, m and f a basket: messoria: aristas Corbe tulit, O.: de corbibus māla, Iu.

corbita.definition: corbīta ae, f corbis, a ship of burden.

cordatus.definition: cordātus adj. cor, wise, prudent, judicious: egregie homo, Enn. ap. C.

cordax.definition: cordax acis, m, ko/rdac (a wanton dance); of the trochee, the dancing metre.

corium.definition: corium ī, n SCAL-, skin, hide, leather: bovis, Ta.: (animantes) coriis tectae: (turrīs) coriis intexerant, Cs.: scuta ex coriis, S.—Prov.: canis a corio numquam absterrebitur uncto, i. e. habits stick closely, H.

corneolus.definition: 'corneolus adj. dim. 1 corneus, horny, of horn: introitus (auris).'

corneus1.definition: 'corneus adj. cornu, of horn, horny: rostrum: arcus, O.: porta Somni, V.'

corneus2.definition: corneus adj. 1 cornus, of the cornel-tree: virgulta, V.—Of cornel-wood: hastilia, V., O.

cornicen.definition: cornicen cinis, m cornu + 1 CAN-, a hornblower, trumpeter, cornet-player, C., S., L., Iu.

cornicula.definition: cornīcula ae, f dim. cornix, a little crow, H.

corniculum.definition: corniculum ī, n dim. cornu, a little horn, a horn-shaped ornament (on a helmet), L.

corniger.definition: corniger gera, gerum, adj. cornu + GES-, having horns, horned (poet.): cervi, O.: fluvius, the river-god, V.—As subst m., the river-god Numicius, O.

cornipes.definition: cornipēs pedis, adj. cornu+pes, horn-footed, hoofed (poet.): equi, V., Ct., O.

cornix.definition: cornīx īcis, f 1 CAL-, CAR-, a crow: garrula, O.: Annosa, H.: novem saecula passa, O.: sinistra (a favorable omen), V.—Prov.: cornicum oculos configere, i. e. catch a weasel asleep.

cornu.definition: cornū ūs (acc. cornum, T., O.), n (once m, C.) 1 CAR-, a horn, antler: (animantes) cornibus armatae: tauri, O.: cornu ferit (caper), V.: luctantur cornibus haedi, V.—As a vessel: bilibre, H.—As a funnel: inserto latic…

cornum1.definition: cornum ī, n 1 cornus, the cornel-berry, cornel-cherry, V., H., O. — A javelin (of cornelwood), O.

cornus.definition: cornus ī (abl. cornū, O.), f 1 CAR-, a cornel cherry-tree, V.— Cornel-wood, O.—A javelin (of cornel-wood), V., O.

corolla.definition: corōlla ae, f a little crown or garland, Ct., Tb.

corollarium.definition: corōllārium ī, n corolla (prop., a garland), a gift, present, douceur, gratuity: sine corollario discedere: nummorum.

corona.definition: corōna ae, f, korw/nh, a garland, chaplet, wreath: coronam habere in capite: virtute parta: laurea, L.: Necte Lamiae coronam, H.—Worn in offering sacrifice: Insignis gemmis, V.: tenuis, Iu. —A crown, diadem: duplex ge…

coronarius.definition: corōnārius adj. corona, for a crown: aurum, crown money (levied for a victorious general).

corono.definition: corōnō āvī, ātus, āre corona, to furnish with a garland, crown, wreathe: sedebat coronatus: templa, O.: deos fragili myrto, H.: vina, V.: epulae inibant coronati: alqm fronde, H.: coronatus malobathro capillos, H.: co…

corporeus.definition: corporeus adj. corpus, of the body, physical: (ignis): pestes, ills, V.— Of flesh, fleshly: umerus, O.: dapes, O.—Corporeal, substantial: res.

corpus.definition: corpus oris, n 1 CER-, a body (living or lifeless): solidum et suci plenum, T.: requies animi et corporis: ingenium sine corpore exercere, S.: corpus sine pectore, H.: Corporis exigui, of small frame, H.: dedit pro co…

corpusculum.definition: corpusculum ī, n dim. corpus, a puny body: quantula hominum, Iu.— An atom, particle.

corrado.definition: corrādō (conr-) sī, sus, ere com- + rado, to scrape together, rake up: Minas alicunde, T.: ei munus hoc, for her, T.: omnia (for sale), T.

correctio.definition: corrēctiō (conr-) ōnis, f corrigo, an amendment, improvement, correction: philosophiae: correctione gaudere. — In rhet., a restatement, repetition in better language.

corrector.definition: corrēctor (conr-) ōris, m corrigo, an amender, improver, reformer: civitatis: Corrector! T.—A censor, reprover: asperitatis, H.: noster: Bestius, i. e. a preacher of morals, H.

correpo.definition: corrēpō (con-r-) psī, —, ere, to creep, slink: in aliquam onerariam.—Fig.: in dumeta, to take to the bush (i. e. unintelligible arguments).

correpte.definition: (correptē) adv. correptus, shortly.—Only comp: (syllaba) correptius exit, i. e. in a short vowel, O.

corrigia.definition: corrigia (conr-) ae, f a shoe-tie, shoe-latchet.

corrigo.definition: corrigō (conr-) rēxī, rēctus, ere com- + rego, to make straight, set right, bring into order: correctis ceris, smoothed out, O.: cursum (navis), L. —Fig., to improve, amend, correct, reform, restore: gnatum mi, T.: te…

corripio.definition: corripiō (conr-) ripuī, reptus, ere com- + rapio, to seize, snatch up, grasp, collect, take hold of, arrest: quos corripi atque interfici iussit, Cs.: arcum manu, V.: fascibus conreptis, S.: me, to start up, T.: a som…

corroboro.definition: corrōborō (con-r-) āvī, ātus, āre, to strengthen, invigorate, make strong, corroborate: vox cum se corroborarit: cum is iam se corroboravisset, i. e. was grown up.—Fig., to encourage, fortify, strengthen: virtutem: au…

corrodo.definition: corrōdō (conr-) sī, sus, ere com- + rodo, to gnaw, gnaw to pieces: scuta: ossa, Iu.—To wear away (of a file): ferrum, Ph.

corrogo.definition: corrogō (conr-) āvī, ātus, āre com- + rogo, to bring together by entreaty, collect, drum up, obtain by soliciting: suos necessarios ab atriis: convenerunt conrogati: auxilia ab sociis, L.: vela cum antemnis ex navibus…

corrugo.definition: corrūgō (conr-) —, —, āre com- + rugo, to wrinkle, corrugate: nares, i. e. produce loathing, H.

corrumpo.definition: corrumpō (con-r-) rūpī, ruptus, ere, to destroy, ruin, waste: frumentum in areā: (frumentum) incendio, Cs.: coria igni, Cs.: ungues dentibus, to bite, Pr.: se suasque spes, S.: opportunitates, to lose, S.—To adulterat…

corruo.definition: corruō (conr-) uī, —, ere com- + ruo, to fall together, fall down, fall, tumble, sink: aedes corruerunt: adducta funibus arbor, O.: igne rogus, O.: paene risu: exspirantes corruerunt, L.: quo loco corruerat icta (Hora…

corrupte.definition: corruptē adv. with comp. corruptus, perversely: iudicare: corruptius habiti, i. e. under less restraint, Ta.

corruptela.definition: corruptēla (conr-) ae, f corruptus, a corrupting, corruption, seduction, bribery: mores hac corruptelā depravati: via corruptelae, L.: mulierum: servi.— A seducer, misleader: liberūm, T.

corruptio.definition: corruptiō (conr-) ōnis, f corrumpo, a corrupting, bribery: militum, Ta. — Illness, unsoundness: corporis.—Fig.: opinionum.

corruptor.definition: corruptor (conr-) ōris, m corrumpo, a misleader, seducer, briber: iuventutis: (Matronae), H.: tribūs: amicitiae, a violator, Ta.

corruptrix.definition: corruptrīx (conr-) īcis, f corruptor, one who seduces: tam corruptrice provinciā.

corruptus.definition: corruptus (conr-) adj. with comp. and sup. P. of corrumpo, spoiled, marred, corrupted, bad: hordeum, Cs.: iter factum corruptius imbri, H.— Fig., bad, corrupt: mores, S.: quis corruptus, qui? etc.: iudex, H.: iudicia:…

cortex.definition: cortex icis, m and f 1 CAR-, the bark, rind, shell, hull.—Of plants: obducuntur cortice trunci: scutis ex cortice factis, Cs.: Ora corticibus horrenda cavatis, masks, V.: Sumpta de cortice grana, the hull, O. — The ba…

cortina.definition: cortīna ae, f a kettie, caldron, the tripod of Apollo, in the form of a caldron, V.—The priestess of Apollo: reddidit vocem, O.—A circle of hearers, Ta.

corusco.definition: coruscō —, —, āre coruscus, to move quickly, vibrate, shake, brandish, weave, tremble (poet.): duo Gaesa manu, V.: telum, V.: linguas (colubrae), O.: frontem, toss, Iu.: Cunctanti telum, brandishes at, V.—To be in qui…

coruscus.definition: coruscus adj., in waving motion, waving, vibrating, tremulous: silvae, V.: ilices, V.—Flashing, gleaming, glittering: ignis, H.: vis fulminis, C. poet.: sol, V.: radii (solis), O.: Pyrrhus telis, V.: cristis capita al…

corvus.definition: corvus ī, m 1 CAL-, a raven: loquax, O.: ovantes gutture corvi, V.: hians, H.—As a bird of omen: Oscen, H.: Delius in corvo latuit, O.— Prov.: in cruce corvos pascere, to be hanged, H. —A grappling-iron, Cu.

corycus.definition: cōrycus (cōri-) ī, m, kw/rukos (prop., a sack of sand for athletes), a means of exercise, discipline: laterum et vocis.

coryletum.definition: corylētum or corulētum ī, n corylus, a hazel-thicket, hazel-copse, O.

corylus.definition: corylus or corulus ī, f a hazel-tree, filberttree, V., O.

corymbus.definition: corymbus ī, m, ko/rumbos, a cluster of ivyberries, cluster, garland, V., O., Pr., Iu.

coryphaeus.definition: coryphaeus ī, m, korufai=os, a leader, chief, head: Epicureorum.

corytos.definition: cōrȳtos (gōrȳ-, -tus) ī, m, gwruto/s, a quiver, V., O.

cos.definition: cōs cōtis, f 1 CA-, a flint-stone, whetstone, grindstone: novaculā cotem discissurus, L.: cruenta, H.: subigunt in cote secures, V. — Fig.: iracundiam fortitudinis quasi cotem esse: fungar vice cotis, H.

cosmetes.definition: cosmētēs ae, m, kosmh/ths, an adorner, slave of the wardrobe, Iu.

cosmoe.definition: cosmoe m plur., ko/smoi (only nom.), the ten councillors of state in Crete.

costa.definition: costa ae, f, a rib: per costas eminere, L.: Tergora deripiunt costis, V.: laterum costas verberat, O.—Plur, a side, wall: aheni, V.

costum.definition: costum ī, n, ko/stos, an Oriental aromatic plant, H., O., Pr.

cotes1.definition: cōtēs f 1 CA-, a pointed rock, crag: obnoxia ventis, Tb.: saxa et cautes timere, Cs.: durae, V.: scrupulosae cotes: durae, V.: inviae, Cu.

cothurnatus.definition: cothurnātus adj. cothurnus, with the cothurnus, buskined, tragic: deae, O.

cothurnus.definition: cothurnus ī, m, ko/thornos, a high Grecian shoe: cum pallā et cothurnis.—A laced huntingboot covering the foot, V. — A buskin, high shoe worn by tragic actors, H.: grandes cothurni, i. e. tragedy, H.: Sophocleus, the …

cottidiano.definition: cottīdiānō adv. cottidianus, daily: in forum descendere.

cottidianus.definition: cottīdiānus or cotīdiānus (not quot-), adj. cottidie, of every day, daily: febris, T.: curae: peccata: consuetudo, Cs.: agger, made each day, Cs.: sumptus, N.: usus et cultus corporis, S.— Every day, daily, usual, ord…

cottidie.definition: cottīdiē or cotīdiē (not quot-), adv. quot- + dies, daily, every day: minari: castra movere, S.: summa et cotidie maiora praemia.

cottona.definition: cottona (-ana) ōrum, n, ko/ttana Syriac, small Syrian figs, Iu.

coturnix.definition: coturnīx īcis, f a quail, O., Iu.

covinarius.definition: covīnārius (covinn-) ī, m covīnus, a warchariot, Celtic, a driver of a scythe-chariot, Ta.

coxa.definition: coxa ae, f the hip, Iu.

crabro.definition: crābrō ōnis, m CRAP-, a hornet, V., O.

crambe.definition: crambē ēs, f, kra/mbh, a kind of cabbage. —Prov.: repetita, warmed over, i. e. an old story, Iu.

crapula.definition: crāpula ae, f, kraipa/lh, excessive drinking, intoxication: convivii: crapulae plenus, L.: crapulam edormire: crapulā graves, Cu.

cras.definition: crās adv., to-morrow: rus cras ibo, T.: saga sumentur: donaberis haedo, H.: cras mane, early to-morrow morning: cras est mihi Iudicium, T.— In the future, hereafter (poet.): Quid sit futurum cras, H.: nec quod sumus, …

crasse.definition: crassē adv. crassus, thickly, grossly, rudely: compositum poëma, H.

crassitudo.definition: crassitūdō inis, f crassus, thickness: parietum pedes V, Cs.: in quo (libramento) nulla: fornicum, L.: stipites feminis crassitudine, Cs.— Density: aeris.

crassus.definition: crassus adj. CART-, solid, thick, fat, gross, stout: unguentum, H.: cruor, V.: ager: (homo), T.: toga, H.: filum, O.—Thick, dense, heavy: aër: caelum.— Fig., stolid, dense: Rusticus crassā Minervā, H.

crastinus.definition: crāstinus adj. cras, of to-morrow, to-morrow's: dies: Cynthius, O.: lux, V.: hora, V.: tempora, H.: in crastinum differre, till to-morrow: pervenire, N.

crater.definition: crātēr ēris (acc. -ēra), m, krath/r, a mixingvessel, wine-bowl, punch-bowl (poet.): Sistitur argento crater, O.: vertunt crateras aë nos, V.: urnae capax, holding three gallons, Iu. — A bowl: fuso crateres olivo, V.—T…

cratera.definition: crātēra ae, f, krath/r, a mixing-vessel, winebowl, punch - bowl: pulcherrimae: vetus, H.: dat Crateram Aeneae, O. — A bay near Baiae.— The Bowl (a constellation).

cratis.definition: (crātis is), f CART-, wicker-work, a hurdle: terga suis rarā pendentia crate, kitchen-rack, Iu.: cratīs texunt virgis, V.: Claudens textis cratibus pecus, H.—A harrow: vimineae, V.—A hurdle (for drowning criminals): c…

creatio.definition: creātiō ōnis, f creo, an electing, appointment, choice: magistratuum.

creator.definition: creātor ōris, m creo, a creator, author, begetter, founder: urbis: Achillis, father, O.

creatrix.definition: creātrīx īcis, f creator, she who produces, a mother: diva, V.

creber.definition: crēber bra, brum, adj. with comp. crēbrior, and sup. crēberrimus 1 CER-, thick, close, pressed together, frequent, numerous, repeated: arbores, Cs.: (venae) corpore intextae: creberrima aedificia, Cs.: ignes quam creb…

crebra.definition: crēbra adv. plur n. of creber, often, in quick succession: pede terram ferit, V.

crebresco.definition: crēbrēscō bruī, —, ere creber, to become frequent, increase, spread abroad: crebrescunt optatae aurae, V.: horror, V.: sermo, V.: seditio, Ta.: crebrescit vivere Agrippam, it is generally reported, Ta.

crebritas.definition: crēbritās ātis, f creber, thickness, closeness, frequency: litterarum.

crebro.definition: crēbrō adv. with comp. crēbrius, and sup. crēberrimē creber, in quick succession, repeatedly, often, frequently, many times: ruri esse, T.: cum crebro integri defessis succederent, Cs.: personare aurem, H.: alqm nomin…

credibilis.definition: crēdibilis e, adj. credo, to be believed, worthy of belief, likely, credible: Hocine, ut, etc., T.: crimen: narrationes: magnum narras, vix credibile, H.: non est credibile, quid sit, etc.: patiens supra quam cuiquam …

creditor.definition: crēditor ōris, m credo, a creditor: cum creditoribus suis agere: rem creditori solvere, L.: Damasippi, H.

creditum.definition: crēditum ī, n credo, a loan: solvere, L.: abiurare, S.

credo.definition: crēdō didī, ditus, ere CRAT- + 2 DA-, to give as a loan, lend, make a loan: pecunias creditas solvere: quibus pecuniam.—To commit, consign, intrust: alcuius fidei: mihi suom animum, T.: militi arma, L.: se suaque omni…

credulitas.definition: crēdulitās ātis, f credulus, ready belief, credulity, rash confidence: patris, O.: sua, O.

credulus.definition: crēdulus adj. credo, that easily believes, credulous, easy of belief, confiding, unsuspecting: senes: nimis: te fruitur credulus aureā, H.: piscis in undā, O.: illis, V.: postero (diei), H.: in vitium, O.—Trustful, cr…

cremo.definition: cremō āvī, ātus, āre 2 CAR-, to burn, consume by fire: igni cremari, Cs.: urbem, L.: herbas, O.: Visa (est) ornatum flammā cremari, to be ablaze in her head - dress, V. — Of the dead: igni voluit cremari: corpora lign…

cremor.definition: cremor ōris, m a thick vegetable juice, O.

creo.definition: creō āvī (creāssit for creāverit, C.), ātus, āre 1 CER-, to bring forth, produce, make, create, beget, give origin to: Aenean, L.: fortes creantur fortibus, H.: vapor omnīs Res creat, O.: quicquid mortale creamur, who…

crepida.definition: crepida ae, f, krhpi/s, a sandal, sole with straps, half-shoe, Grecian shoe, C., L., H., Cu.

crepido.definition: crepīdō inis, f crepida, a foundation of masonry, base: tamquam crepidine quādam sustineri.—A causeway, mole, pier: omnes urbis: saxi, V.: haud faciliori ascensu, L.: magnae molis, Cu.: Nulla crepido vacat (to beg on)…

crepito.definition: crepitō —, —, āre, freq. crepo, to rattle, creak, crackle, clatter, rustle, rumble, chatter, murmur: tenui rostro, O.: grandine nimbi, V.: crepitans salit grando, V.: sistrum crepitans, Pr.: incudibus enses, to ring, …

crepitus.definition: crepitus ūs, m crepo, a rattling, creaking, clattering, clashing, rustling: dentium. chattering: fulmine Dissultant crepitūs, V.: armorum, L.: plagarum: materiae flagrantis, crackling, L.

crepo.definition: crepō uī, itus, āre CREP-. I. To rattle, crack, creak, rustle, clatter, tinkle, jingle, chink: fores crepuerunt ab eā, T.: crepet laurus adusta, O.: crepante pede, H.: nubes subito motu, O.: sinūs crepantes Carbasei, …

crepundia.definition: crepundia ōrum, n crepo, a child's rattle.

crepusculum.definition: crepusculum ī, n creper, gloomy, twilight, dusk, the evening twilight: sera, O.: crepusculo solutus, Ph. — Dimness, obscurity, dark: iter per opaca crepuscula, O.: dubiae lucis, O.

cresco.definition: crēscō crēvī, crētus, ere, inch. 1 CER-, to come into being, spring up: crescit seges, O.—P. perf., with abl, arisen, descended, born, produced (poet.): mortali semine, O.: Alcanore, V.: ab origine eādem, O.: Troiano …

creta.definition: crēta ae, f Creta, Cretan earth, pipe - clay, chalk, as a cosmetic, H.; for seals, C.; for cement, V.; eaten by serpents, V.: rapidus cretae Oaxes, turbulent, V.: cretā notati, i. e. with a mark of approval, H.

cretatus.definition: crētātus adj. creta, marked with chalk: fasciae: bos (as an offering), Iu.

cretio.definition: crētiō ōnis, f 2 CER-, a formal acceptance of an inheritance.

cretosus.definition: crētōsus adj. creta, abounding in chalk: rura, O.

cretula.definition: crētula ae, f dim. creta, white clay, used for sealing: signum in cretulā .

crevi.definition: crēvī perf. of cerno, and of crēscō.

cribrum.definition: crībrum ī, n 2 CER-, a sieve, riddle, C., O.

crimen.definition: crīmen inis, n 2 CER-, a judgment, charge, accusation, reproach: crimini credidisse, T.: fidem criminibus facere, L.: respondere criminibus: falsis criminibus circumventus, calumnies, S.: fictum, O.: cui crimina noxia…

criminatio.definition: crīminātiō ōnis, f criminor, an accusation, complaint, calumny: criminatione in me uti: tua: speciosa, L.: ab aliquo adlatae.

criminator.definition: crīminātor ōris, m an accuser, slanderer: in alios, Ta.

criminor.definition: crīminor ātus, ārī, dep. crimen, to accuse of crime, complain of, impeach, calumniate: me tibi, T.: apud alqm nos: alios apud populum, L.—To complain of, charge, denounce: potentiam meam invidiose: nescio quid de illā…

criminose.definition: crīminōsē adv. with comp. criminosus, reproachfully, slanderously: de bello loqui, S.: acta res est: criminosius dicere.

criminosus.definition: crīminōsus adj. with comp. crimen, bringing accusations, reproachful, calumniating, slanderous: nomen: id mihi criminosum esse, a reproach: orationes, L.: iambi, H.: criminosior oratio, Her.

crinalis.definition: crīnālis e, adj. crinis, of the hair: vitta, V.: aurum, V.— As subst n., a hair-pin: curvum, O.

crinis.definition: crīnis is, m 2 CEL-, the hair, hair of the head: demisso crine, O.: crinem manibus laniare, O.: mulieri praebere haec in crinīs, hair-money: praesectis crinibus, Cs.: crinibus passis, L.: torti, Ta.: solutis crinibus,…

crinitus.definition: crīnītus adj. crinis, covered with hair, hairy, with flowing locks, long - haired: Iopas, V.: draconibus ora, O.: galea triplici iubā , V.

criso.definition: crīsō (crīssō) āvī, —, āre, to move the haunches, Iu.

crispisulcans.definition: crīspisulcāns adj. crispus + sulco, roughfurrowing, serpentine, Poet. ap. C.

crispo.definition: crīspō —, ātus, āre crispus, to swing, brandish: Bina manu hastilia, V.

crispus.definition: crīspus adj. SCARP-, having curled hair, curly-headed, T. — Curled, uneven, waving, wrinkled: parietes abiete crispā, Enn. ap. C.—Quivering, tremulous: pecten, Iu.

crista.definition: crista ae, f 2 CEL-, a tuft, comb, crest, Iu.— Of a lapwing, O.: anguis cristis praesignis, a golden crest, O.: cristis aureus deus, O.: illi surgunt cristae, he carries his head high, Iu.—Of a helmet, a crest, plume,…

cristatus.definition: cristātus adj. crista, tufted, crested: ales, O.: draco, O.— Crested, plumed: cassis pennis, O.: galeae, L.: Achilles, V.

criticus.definition: criticus ī, m, kritiko/s, a judge, critic, C., H.

croceus.definition: croceus adj. crocus, of saffron, saffron-colored, yellow, golden: odores, V.: flores, V.—Saffron: Tithoni cubile, V.: amictus, O.: fetus (visci), V.

crocinus.definition: crocinus adj., krokino/s, of saffron: tunica, saffron-colored, Ct.— As subst n., saffron-oil, Pr.

crocodilus.definition: crocodīlus (C., H., Iu.) or corcodīlus (Ph.), ī, m, kroko/deilos, a crocodile.

crocota.definition: crocōta ae, f, krokwto/s, a saffron-colored dress, court dress (for a woman).

crotalistria.definition: crotalistria ae, f a castanet dancer, Pr.

crotalum.definition: crotalum ī, n, kro/talon, a rattle, bell, castanet.

cruciamentum.definition: cruciāmentum ī, n crucio, torture, torment: carnificum.

cruciatus2.definition: cruciātus m crucio, torture, torment, a torturing, execution: in cruciatum abripi, T.: in eos cruciatūs edere, Cs.: in dolore cruciatuque moriens: animi cruciatūs et corporis.—Plur, instruments of torture: laminae cet…

crucio.definition: cruciō āvī, ātus, āre crux, to put to the rack, torture, torment: fame cruciari: tribunos cruciando occidit, L.: cum cruciabere Sanguine serpentis, O.—Fig., to afflict, grieve, torment: graviter adulescentulum, T.: se…

crudelis.definition: crūdēlis e, adj. with comp. and sup. crudus, rude, unfeeling, hard, unmerciful, hard - hearted, cruel, severe, fierce: mulier: in calamitate hominis: cenatus in conservandā patriā: in eos: in patriam: gratuito, S.: ec…

crudelitas.definition: crūdēlitās ātis, f crudelis, harshness, severity, cruelty, barbarity: in homines: in immanitate puniendā: erga nobiles, N.: alicuius crudelitatem horrere, Cs.: esse singulari crudelitate: crudelitatem exercere in vivo…

crudeliter.definition: crūdēliter adv. with comp. and sup. crudelis, cruelly, fiercely, in a cruel manner, C.: excruciatus, Cs.: victoriam exercebant, S.: crudelius factum: amare, O.: supplicium crudelissime sumere.

crudesco.definition: crūdēscō duī, —, ere, inch. crudus, to increase in violence, be aggravated, grow worse: coepit crudescere morbus, V.: seditio, Ta.

cruditas.definition: crūditās ātis, f crudus, an overloading of the stomach.

crudus.definition: crūdus adj. with comp. CRV-, bloody, bleeding, trickling with blood: volnera, O.: exta, L.— With full stomach, stuffed with food, dyspeptic: qui de conviviis auferantur crudi: pilā ludere inimicum crudis, H.: (homo) c…

cruento.definition: cruentō āvī, ātus, āre cruentus, to make bloody, spot with blood, stain, cause to bleed: manūs sanguine, N.: mensam sanguine, L.: gladium in pugnā, S.: ōs, O.: cruentati redeunt, O.—Fig., to wound: haec te cruentat or…

cruentus.definition: cruentus adj. CRV-, spotted with blood, bloody, stained: sanguine civium: sanguine fraterno, H.: cadaver: vehiculum, L.: manūs, S.— Plur n. as subst: gaudens Bellona cruentis, in gory deeds, H.—Delighting in blood, bl…

crumena.definition: crumēna (-mīna) ae, f SCRV-, a moneybag, purse: non deficiente crumenā, H., Iu.

cruor.definition: cruor ōris, m CRV-, blood, bloodshed, gore, a stream of blood: inimici recentissimus: cruore omnia conpleri, S.: cruor emicat alte, O.: viperinus, H.: siccabat veste cruores, blood-stains, V.: arma uncta cruoribus, H.…

cruppellarii.definition: cruppellāriī ōrum Celtic, among the Gauls, armored foot-soldiers, Ta.

crus.definition: crūs ūris, n 1 CEL-, the leg, shank, shin: crura suffringere: dimidium, broken, Iu.: medium impediit crus Pellibus, H.: (equus) iactat crura, V.— The legs of crucified criminals were broken; hence, prov.: perire eum n…

crusta.definition: crūsta ae, f CRV-, a hard surface, rind, shell, crust, bark: fluminis, a crust of ice, V.—Inlaid work, chasing, embossed work, stucco, mosaic: eis (vasis) crustae detrahebantur: capaces Heliadum crustae, chased cups, Iu.

crustulum.definition: crūstulum ī, n dim. crustum, small pastry, confectionery: pueris dare crustula, H., Iu.

crustum.definition: crūstum ī, n CRV-, a hard loaf, cake, pastry: Crustis viduas venari, H.: fatale, V.

crux.definition: crux ucis, f CVR-, a gallows, frame, tree (on which criminals were impaled or hanged), C.—A cross: (mereri) crucem, T.: cruci suffixi: in crucem acti, S.: Non pasces in cruce corvos, H.: pretium sceleris, Iu.—Torture,…

crypta.definition: crypta ae, f, kru/pth, a vault, cavern, Iu.

crystallinum.definition: crystallinum ī, n, krusta/llinon (sc. vas), a crystalline vase: grandia, Iu.

crystallus.definition: crystallus ī, f, kru/stallos, a crystal: imago Solis crystallo inclusa, Cu.: aquosa, Pr.

cubicularis.definition: cubiculāris e, adj. cubiculum, of a sleepingchamber: lectus.

cubicularius.definition: cubiculārius m cubiculum, a chamber-servant, valet-de-chambre.

cubiculum.definition: cubiculum ī, n cubo, a room for reclining, sleeping - chamber, bedchamber: altum: exire de cubiculo: principum feminarum, Ta.

cubile.definition: cubīle is, n CVB-, a place of rest, couch, bed: suum: filiae: (Fennis) cubile humus, Ta.: patrium, O.—The marriage bed: viduum, O.: sociare cubilia cum alqo, contract marriage, O.—A nest, lair, hole, kennel; of the vu…

cubital.definition: cubital ālis, n cubitum, a cushion, elbowcushion, H.

cubitalis.definition: cubitālis e, adj. cubitum, of a cubit, L.

cubito.definition: cubitō āvī, —, āre, freq. cubo, to lie down often, be accustomed to lie: tecum semper.

cubitum.definition: cubitum ī, n (rarely cubitus, ī, m) CVB-, the elbow: cubito adnixa, V.: cubito presso, H.: in cubitum se reponet, lean upon, H.: cubiti frangit Ossa, O.: ferit (me) cubito, jogs, Iu. — The arm: cubiti sinuantur in ala…

cubo.definition: cubō uī (subj. cubāris, Pr.), itum, āre CVB-, to lie down, recline: in lecticā: argenteis lectis, Cu.: in spondā, H.: in faciem (opp. supinus), Iu. —To lie asleep, sleep: cubitum ire.—To recline at table: nemo gustavi…

cubus.definition: cubus ī, m, ku/bos, a mass, quantity: modicus, O.

cucullus1.definition: cucullus ī, m 2 CAL-, a hood, cowl, cap on a cloak, Iu.

cucullus2.definition: cucūllus (-ūlus) ī, m a cuckoo, H.

cucumis.definition: cucumis eris, m a cucumber, V.

cucurbita.definition: cucurbita ae, f (prop., a gourd), a cuppingglass (from its form), Iu.

cudo.definition: cūdō —, —, ere, to strike, beat, pound, knock. —Prov.: istaec in me cudetur faba, i. e. I shall smart for that, T. — To hammer, stamp, coin: argentum, T.

cuias.definition: cūiās ātis, pron interrog. 2 CA-, whence? of what country? from what place? quis et cuias, L.: cuiatem se esse diceret.

cuicuimodi.definition: cuicuimodī adv. euphon. for cuiuscuiusmodi; gen. of quisquis + modus, of whatever kind, of what sort soever: cuicuimodi es: sunt.

cuius.definition: cūius (old quōius) adj. 2 CA- —Interrog., of whom? whose? virgo quoiast? T.: cuium pecus? an Meliboei? V.—Relat., of whom, whose: is, cuia res sit.

cuiusdam.definition: cūiusdam modī, cūius modī, cūiusque modī see quidam, quis, quisque.

culcita.definition: culcita ae, f a bed, cushion, pillow.

culex.definition: culex icis, m a gnat, midge, H.

culina.definition: culīna ae, f 2 CAR-, a kitchen: vetus, H.— A table, food: praebens culinam, H.: nidor culinae, Iu.: magna, splendid, Iu.

culleus.definition: culleus (cūleus), ī, m, koleo/s (Ion. kouleo/s), a leather bag, sack for liquids, N. — Parricides were sewed up in bags and drowned: insutus in culeum, C., Iu.

culmen.definition: culmen inis, n for columen, the top, summit, roof, gable: mersae culmina villae, O.: tuguri, V.: aedis, L.: culmina hominum, deorum, i. e. of houses and temples, V.: Alpium, Cs.: summum hominis, the crown of the head,…
